body:
[ stdin# ]Our Revolution Logo

LIVE with Sen. Chris Van Hollen: The Fight for New Senate Leadership!

Peter Willis,

The Blue Wave was powered by a Progressive Earthquake that helped
Democrats win back the House and Senate. Now comes the next big fight:
making sure our new majority has the bold leadership to deliver for
working people.

This Monday, Nov. 23, at 8:30 PM ET, join Our Revolution and MoveOn for a
special LIVE Leadership for Change Town Hall with Sen. Chris Van Hollen!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40160?t=1011&akid=11628%2E5885482%2ENHTNYj ]RSVP NOW: JOIN OUR LIVE TOWN HALL WITH SEN. CHRIS VAN HOLLEN!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40160?t=1012&akid=11628%2E5885482%2ENHTNYj ]RSVP NOW

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40160?t=1013&akid=11628%2E5885482%2ENHTNYj ]Graphic with a picture of Van Hollen reading: LEADERSHIP FOR CHANGE
TOWN HALL WITH SEN. CHRIS VAN HOLLEN. NOV. 23 @ 8:30p ET / 5:30 PT

Our Revolution is proud to endorse Sen. Chris Van Hollen for Senate
Majority Leader. And we’re mobilizing our grassroots movement to make sure
senators hear the call for change.

Why Van Hollen? Because he’s shown he’s willing to take on powerful
interests — including those within his own party.

He’s fighting to crack down on corruption and the influence of federal
contractors who bankroll political campaigns. He’s challenging the
expansion of U.S.-Israel military integration and pushing to strip Section
219 from the National Defense Authorization Act.

And he’s a longtime champion of Medicare for All.

That’s the kind of leadership this moment demands. Someone willing to
stand up to corporate power, challenge the political establishment, and
fight for the issues that matter most to working people: affordable
healthcare, getting big money out of politics, ending endless wars, and
stopping more bombs for Israel.

In our new survey, nearly 75% of you told us you want to see a new Senate
Majority Leader. Well, this is our chance.

At Monday’s LIVE town hall, we’ll hear directly from Sen. Van Hollen about
what’s at stake in the Senate leadership fight, his vision for the new
Democratic majority, and how our grassroots movement can help shape what
comes next.

We’ll also be joined by leaders from MoveOn, the International Association
of Machinists union, Sunrise Movement, Friends of the Earth Action, and
Progressive Maryland as we build momentum for a new era of politics in
America.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40160?t=1014&akid=11628%2E5885482%2ENHTNYj ]RSVP HERE: LEADERSHIP FOR CHANGE TOWN HALL — MONDAY, NOV. 23, AT 8:30
PM ET / 5:30 PM PT!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40160?t=1015&akid=11628%2E5885482%2ENHTNYj ]RSVP NOW

Our movement fought hard to win this majority. Now we have to make it
deliver.

The voters sent a clear message on Election Day: We’re ready for change.
And that means new leadership willing to take on Trump, the billionaires,
and the corporate interests standing in the way of progress.

Let’s turn our Progressive Earthquake into a new era of leadership in
Washington.

When we organize, we win.

Our Revolution

P.S. Winning the majority was just the beginning. Now we’re taking on the
party establishment to make sure Democrats deliver on the progressive
agenda voters demanded. [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40161?t=1016&akid=11628%2E5885482%2ENHTNYj ]Can you chip in $5, $10, or whatever you can
today to power our grassroots fight for bold new leadership? Every
contribution helps us organize, mobilize, and hold Democrats accountable.
Thank you.

body:
Last night, more than 750 members of the Swing Left community showed up for our Inside Update call.
#
What a night!
Last night, more than 750 members of the Swing Left community showed up for our Inside Update call. People joined from all over the country, and the energy was _incredible_. Together, we celebrated the historic wins from Election Night, our work together, and how much this crew of relentless grassroots donors, volunteers, organizers, and leaders accomplished.
Our personal favorite? _“When do we start canvassing again?”_
If you missed the call, here’s a quick recap of what we covered.
**How Ground Truth data was utilized**
One of the biggest lessons from Ground Truth is that campaigns are overlooking voters they could win, and it was really exciting to see how candidates and campaigns used the information shared through these conversations. Here are some of the examples shared:
* **Followed up directly with voters.** Candidates like Representative Janelle Bynum (OR-05), Greg Landsman (OH-01), and Derek Tran (CA-45) personally called undecided voters volunteers had spoken with. Other campaigns added undecided voters into their own outreach programs, including text messages tailored to the specific issues each person had raised.

* **Found issues that weren’t showing up elsewhere.** In one Michigan district, volunteers repeatedly heard concerns about a rusted water tower and the local water supply. It was an issue the candidate hadn’t heard about through other channels yet.

* **Reached voters outside their usual outreach.** A Minnesota campaign had Ground Truth volunteers talk with people in an area their TV ads weren’t reaching.

* **Changed their approach to targeting.** In Oregon, Congresswoman Janelle Bynum’s campaign used Ground Truth findings to broaden its outreach. Her campaign manager told us, “Ground Truth’s initial efforts showed us the evidence we needed to broaden our outreach beyond traditional narrow voter targeting.”

**The moment we’re in**
On Election Day, voters sent a clear message. And while it was a resounding rejection of Donald Trump and his Republican allies in Congress and in the states, many of the people we talked to this fall aren’t loyal Democrats.
While the gains Democrats made were very real, they’re also fragile. In 2028, Trump won’t be on the ballot to vote against. Democrats will have to give people something to vote _for._
We need to keep this year's new Democratic voters, reach voters Democrats have overlooked or written off, and keep convincing people who don’t yet agree with us.
**What it will take**
Over the next two years, we need to **show that Democratic governance makes people’s lives better.** That means delivering tangible policy wins, both in Congress and in the states where Democrats won governing power this year (all 30 of them, starting in January!)
We’re also going to **need to hold Republican leaders accountable.** That means taking real action against corrupt officials in the Trump administration—and the good news is that Democrats are now in a position to do exactly that, with large majorities in both the House and Senate.
Additionally, we need to build on what we started this year with Ground Truth. That means **doing the slow, patient work of listening and changing minds.**
Plus, we need to **build campaigns around volunteers, not as an afterthought.** People power is something money can’t buy, and it can’t be switched on and off each cycle. Volunteers can reach more voters and build relationships at a scale paid field programs can’t.
Finally, **we need to start building for 2028 _now_**. A crowded presidential primary could leave the nominee with very little time to build a general election campaign. The groundwork has to be laid now, for whoever wins.
**How Swing Left will get there**
Our focus, starting now, is winning in 2028. We’ll get there by:
* Growing our volunteer groups to continue training and developing new leaders, and building a community of volunteers who show up for this work and each other, again and again.
* Working with presidential campaigns during the primaries to share what we learned this year about listening, persuasion, and data (while ultimately remaining neutral on which candidate should win the nomination).
* Working to make sure what you hear keeps reaching campaigns. We built new systems this year for sharing that data, and we’ll keep making them better.
* Raising early money for the House and Senate races that will decide the balance of power.

**From elections to governance**
In addition, volunteers will be at the front lines of connecting constituents to their representatives. Voters shared they want a government that listens and delivers, which means continuing to show up between elections, listen to people, hear their concerns, and help them connect with their representatives. Swing Left’s nonpartisan affiliate Vote Forward will create opportunities for volunteers to engage communities between elections through two complementary programs in 2027.
[**Want to hear more? RSVP for Vote Forward’s Inside Update call, which will be held on Monday, November 23rd at 5 PM PT / 8 PM ET.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/3314?t=1&akid=3465%2E1562180%2E2YUoxZ)
**Ready to take action?**
After every election, campaigns shut down, and the relationships fade. This time we’re going to keep them going.
We’re offering a winter training program to carry us into the new year. It’s the first step toward 2027 and beyond, where we’ll go back to the basics of organizing—what it is, why it works, and how you can get started even if you’re new to this work.
[**Interested in joining? Apply to join the cohort today.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/3315?t=2&akid=3465%2E1562180%2E2YUoxZ)
Thank you for showing up this year,
The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20261120-1&t=3&refcode2=3465_1562180_2YUoxZ&akid=3465%2E1562180%2E2YUoxZ)

### **Help us beat and replace the mainstream media! Support PolitiBrawl by becoming a paid subscriber today:**
[ Support Our Journalism](https://substack.com/redirect/2666116d-c2a7-48f2-bc3d-5765528f60e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
Texas Republicans are madder than a wet hen, and another fundraising email is not going to improve their disposition.
They have every right to be angry. Voters worked, donated, defended their convictions, and put Republicans in office. Leadership now owes them an explanation that goes considerably further than "It was a difficult political environment."
Yes. Governing is difficult. So is running a business, raising children, and paying the bills. Somehow, the people funding Washington are still expected to perform.
Last week, **["Where the Hell Are the Republicans We Elected?"](https://substack.com/redirect/72206ddf-019a-4f8e-84cf-4326db229fa9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** asked what Republican leadership had done with the opportunity Americans gave it.
The follow-up starts in Texas.
## **Hino who?**
Gina Hinojosa. The Democratic gubernatorial candidate whose reported Texas vote total exceeded Kamala Harris's presidential total by nearly 396,000 votes.
Harris received **[4,835,250 Texas votes in 2024](https://substack.com/redirect/402bd11d-0ac3-4daf-b22d-e309f00c0357?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[.](https://substack.com/redirect/402bd11d-0ac3-4daf-b22d-e309f00c0357?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) The state's reported 2026 results show **[5,230,789 for Hinojosa](https://substack.com/redirect/090b0355-5e5c-46a5-a3d9-7606d8bd0863?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and **5,444,982 for Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico**. Harris's figure is certified; statewide certification of the 2026 results remains pending.
Hinojosa exceeded Harris by 8.2%. Talarico exceeded her by **12.6%** , approximately 610,000 votes.
Meanwhile, approximately **[9.89 million votes](https://substack.com/redirect/090b0355-5e5c-46a5-a3d9-7606d8bd0863?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** were reported in the Senate contest, compared with **[11.39 million in the 2024 presidential contest](https://substack.com/redirect/402bd11d-0ac3-4daf-b22d-e309f00c0357?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. Democratic candidate totals increased while participation in those contests declined.
That is a substantial change. It deserves more than a shrug.
Texas entered the election with approximately **[19.04 million registered voters](https://substack.com/redirect/8fdbbb71-1078-4ef4-9e73-e7851f18d1b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[.](https://substack.com/redirect/8fdbbb71-1078-4ef4-9e73-e7851f18d1b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) The reported Senate vote represents roughly **51.9%** of that electorate. Talarico received votes from approximately **28.6% of all registered voters** , and Hinojosa approximately **27.5%**. Those groups overlap because a voter could support both.
The overall turnout is not unprecedented. Texas reached approximately 53% in 2018, when Beto O'Rourke also exceeded Hillary Clinton's preceding presidential total. The basic pattern has happened before. That does not explain this year's larger increases.
Which counties produced them? What happened at the precinct level? How much reflects crossover voting, new participants, or voters returning after sitting out 2024?
Republicans staying home could explain Republican losses. By itself, it does not explain additional Democratic votes.
"Voters were angry" is a starting point for analysis. It is not the completed assignment.
**PolitiBrawl is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support our work, please consider becoming a paid subscriber.**
[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack..cw2pAMH2kCw6TMoYneDs0mbXAXaq8bg7Y5d35b16HTY?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=225798056)
## **Texas is auditing. What is it checking?**
Texas's first statewide risk-limiting audit began **[November 19](https://substack.com/redirect/9e5f42c3-46ed-47b0-ab0b-75767bc5aa96?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , examining the Senate contest. Officials compare randomly selected paper ballots with reported results. Additional sample hand counts cover the Senate race, Texas Supreme Court chief justice, and another contested race selected locally. These checks were required under existing law.
Good. But a ballot can be counted correctly without that audit establishing whether an eligible voter cast it.
The count and voter eligibility require separate verification.
On September 15, Texas referred **[117 potential noncitizen-voting cases](https://substack.com/redirect/190cd73b-bf75-4ab9-9286-699ec26a3f63?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to the attorney general. Those referrals predate November 3. They are not 117 proven cases from these midterms.
What happened to them? How many were substantiated? Were ineligible registrations removed? Did anyone involved vote this November?
An investigation announcement is not a lifetime exemption from reporting the outcome.
Accuracy must also protect eligible Americans. Texas subsequently established citizenship for **[578 people initially flagged as potential noncitizens](https://substack.com/redirect/190cd73b-bf75-4ab9-9286-699ec26a3f63?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and directed counties to restore registrations incorrectly removed. Citizens should not lose their rights because government records failed to catch up with reality.
Texas has also announced an independent assessment of **[TEAM, its voter-registration management system](https://substack.com/redirect/7c5db0f4-045a-4b2b-90dc-d8f0d31a2b73?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , after county officials complained about performance and processing problems. Reporting describes that assessment as expected to begin in December, alongside working groups to improve the system.
That concerns registration administration, not a finding that voting machines changed totals. But county officials had been raising concerns long before Election Day. The timing deserves an explanation.
_**(Piece continues below)**_
* * *
# **We 're not giving up this fight, and neither should you**
The midterms were a wake up call to all American patriots...
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2666116d-c2a7-48f2-bc3d-5765528f60e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The battle ahead will surely be hard and up-hill. But think of the brave Americans who stormed the beaches of Normandy, or the men who fought and bled at Shiloh and Lexington.
They had a dream for America they were willing to die for. We cannot let their sacrifice be in vain.
This is what we believe in.
We must fight for our nation with everything we've got, even on the darkest days, as our ancestors did.
### **PolitiBrawl will hold our place in line on the battleground for information and news.**
We appreciate your readership and support.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..cw2pAMH2kCw6TMoYneDs0mbXAXaq8bg7Y5d35b16HTY?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=225798056)
Do not give up hope. Tomorrow is a brighter day.
_-The PolitiBrawl Editors_
* * *
_**(Piece continues):**_
## **There is work underway outside government**
The **[Public Interest Legal Foundation](https://substack.com/redirect/c4788d6f-4f84-4a02-be35-03e517253f41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** filed an October 26 administrative complaint alleging **1,057 potential duplicate-registration cases across 22 South Texas counties** , along with hundreds of records containing apparently fictitious birth dates. It requested investigation and corrective action.
Duplicate registrations do not automatically mean duplicate votes. Investigators need to determine what those records represent and whether anyone voted unlawfully.
**[True the Vote](https://substack.com/redirect/4f0ddb77-d833-4b74-8229-3ba36f317bd4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** announced Texas organizing, an audit-information guide, and voter-roll review workshops scheduled to begin November 17. That is concrete organizing and training. Any findings developed through it still need documentation and independent scrutiny.
The Potter County Republican Party's statewide hand-count lawsuit also remains part of the picture. The elections administrator filed a second dismissal motion **[November 19](https://substack.com/redirect/92ebf274-af1f-4e7b-bec1-08e9c36cc593?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , following an amended complaint. The earlier dismissal motion was denied as moot because of that amendment, not because a judge found fraud.
These efforts give officials specific issues to address. Their value will depend on what the evidence establishes.
## **Kansas is red. Do not gloss over that.**
Trump carried Kansas by approximately **[16 percentage points in 2024](https://substack.com/redirect/de11f357-7e35-4fd8-91fc-14c2a1e30be0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[.](https://substack.com/redirect/de11f357-7e35-4fd8-91fc-14c2a1e30be0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Adam Hamilton's reported Senate victory would make him the first Democrat elected to that chamber from Kansas since 1932.
That is a remarkable political reversal.
Kansas has elected Democratic governors, including outgoing Governor Laura Kelly. That helps contextualize the governor's race. It does not explain the Senate result.
The state's unofficial results page, last updated November 8, lists **[561,143 votes for Hamilton](https://substack.com/redirect/7d24c35f-4458-4a75-9a1e-914be0e5aeda?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and **551,243 for Cindy Holscher** , compared with Harris's certified **[544,853 in 2024](https://substack.com/redirect/d4f0c13f-a94d-4053-9b0e-e6de8ea8a278?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. Both exceed Harris, although by substantially smaller percentages than the Texas candidates.
On November 17, Secretary of State Scott Schwab announced that **[all 105 counties had completed their audits and county canvasses](https://substack.com/redirect/4401e30f-5ca3-4eee-8bb6-7269e1e2892b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , including expanded close-race audits for three statewide and three legislative contests. Statewide certification is scheduled for December 1.
Those findings matter. So does an explanation of the political shift grounded in county records.
Calling the result a "wave" gives the outcome a name. It does not explain how it happened.
## **Nevada cannot keep outsourcing its candidates ' appeal to Trump**
Nevada is notorious for plenty of things. An abundance of exceptional political candidates is not among them.
Lombardo blew an opportunity. He governed with Democratic majorities in both the Assembly and Senate, which **[limited what he could accomplish.](https://substack.com/redirect/2c494a8c-ad68-48fb-bb4c-b81449c6a5dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** That deserves acknowledgment. It does not give him a permanent exemption from accountability for his own leadership.
A respected sheriff still has to become an effective governor. Republicans cannot keep recycling familiar names and expecting voters to supply the enthusiasm the candidates fail to earn.
"Look how bad the Democrat is" does not tell a family what the Republican will do for them.
And Trump cannot do everybody's job. His support cannot substitute for a candidate's judgment, record, preparation, or ability to connect with voters. If the entire campaign depends on someone else being compelling, there is a problem with the candidate.
Clark County's results deserve **[an accurate baseline.](https://substack.com/redirect/31753296-7ecb-4cf5-b206-545fd20818d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Lombardo also lost Clark in 2022, when he won statewide. **[Published 2026 county returns](https://substack.com/redirect/265ae7b3-30d8-4f9d-9249-c7770878a45c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** show his deficit widening substantially. That calls for examining turnout, support, and campaign performance rather than assuming Clark had previously voted for him as governor.
**[Washoe County certified its results](https://substack.com/redirect/5289a373-514a-4e40-b9d5-f5190324ed56?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** November 13 by a 3-2 vote. Federal prosecutors separately announced an illegal-voting charge October 23, but that allegation **[concerns 2024](https://substack.com/redirect/a3b60b24-2303-49ec-bfc4-02706c8547f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , not these midterms. Neither a divided certification vote nor an earlier criminal allegation establishes misconduct in this election.
Nevada Republicans need to confront their own choices before asking voters to rescue them from the consequences.

## **Ohio and Arizona require their own examination**
The Texas numerical comparison cannot honestly be pasted onto every Republican loss.
Published returns for Aaron Ford in Nevada, Amy Acton and Sherrod Brown in Ohio, and Katie Hobbs in Arizona are all below Harris's respective 2024 state totals. Those 2026 returns remain subject to their official processes.
The questions need to fit the evidence.
In Ohio, Secretary of State Frank LaRose announced the removal of **[75 additional noncitizen registrations](https://substack.com/redirect/93c926fe-4411-41ee-ae1a-7fde7acd3887?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** before Election Day. Ohio's canvass directive requires reconciliation with pollbooks and registration records to ensure one ballot per voter, along with reconciliation of absentee records and physical ballots. County certification is due November 24.
The completed reconciliation work should demonstrate whether those requirements were fulfilled and how discrepancies were resolved.
In Arizona, the U.S. attorney's office announced **[an October 30 inquiry into allegations](https://substack.com/redirect/8f6d943b-c8c4-4ce3-9a93-017ce5130abd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** involving three nonprofit registration groups and referred the matter to the FBI. Reporting has questioned the underlying evidence. No public finding establishing resulting illegal ballots was located for this update.
Arizona has also posted completed sample hand-count audits for all 15 counties, **[reporting either no discrepancies](https://substack.com/redirect/2728a5b5-33af-497c-be6a-4fc69c3bc7d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** or discrepancies within the permitted margin. Maricopa certified November 18 and identified **[a required recount](https://substack.com/redirect/f8bd17d9-67c0-4f33-90e7-d7ec2896f1a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in Legislative District 27 because of its narrow margin.
Those results belong in the account, whether they please Republican voters or not.
## **Alaska and Mississippi**
Alaska's Senate controversy involved a second candidate with a name similar to incumbent Dan Sullivan's.
**Last night, November 19** , the Justice Department asked the appeals court to treat its challenge **[as moot.](https://substack.com/redirect/53f2fb5e-3398-4057-9406-11069e78ad63?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Mary Peltola had won an outright majority, and her margin exceeded the votes received by the second Sullivan. Alaska lists November 25 as its **[target certification date.](https://substack.com/redirect/9cfcc31c-3467-4fe3-97e6-686f50386886?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
That development must accompany the original allegations. Reporting cannot stop at the moment most convenient to a political argument.
In **[Mississippi](https://substack.com/redirect/9f3f9eff-9af7-4ec1-8a1c-8ddc54bb51fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , Scott Colom's Senate victory was another major upset. Hyde-Smith's lawyers sought **[preservation and separation of affidavit ballots](https://substack.com/redirect/a9056a94-7f32-4554-9f10-1b0a3f13a464?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , the state's provisional ballots. Mississippi has no ordinary automatic or candidate-requested recount process; ballot examinations and legal challenges provide other avenues.
Preserving records makes examination possible. It does not establish that the ballots were unlawful.
## **South Carolina was a failure of Republican judgment**
Darline Graham appears to be a lovely woman. That does not make handing her the political burden of her larger-than-life brother's Senate seat a wise decision, particularly while she was grieving.
This was **[a loss I saw coming.](https://substack.com/redirect/082f0d7c-3d9a-441c-abc2-5792de36fcc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** I have never been a fan of political nepotism, and this was an enormous responsibility to place on someone confronting a personal tragedy. Whoever thought it was good for her, good for South Carolina, and good electoral strategy owes an explanation.
It was unkind to her and foolish politically. Republicans had an opportunity to choose someone whose experience, preparation, and ability to win justified the responsibility. A familiar surname should never have been the deciding qualification.
Annie Andrews won. South Carolina certified its statewide election November 11.
A preventable political mistake does not need a fraud explanation. It needs accountability.

## **Iowa found an actual error and corrected it**
Officials identified approximately **[2,017 absentee ballots omitted from Johnson County's election-night results](https://substack.com/redirect/2ca3dcf1-9be7-4cdd-9c6a-84a07a6fb88b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. The secretary of state directed an audit of the absentee precinct. The county subsequently reported completing the count, maintaining ballot security, and finding **[no changed outcomes](https://substack.com/redirect/bce2069b-a0bc-4c4b-9f35-900704a9bc9c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. It also announced procedural changes.
Overlooking that many ballots deserves scrutiny. Leaving out the correction would mislead readers.
Both facts belong in the story.
## **Now, about those promises**
The House **[passed the SAVE Act](https://substack.com/redirect/1528cadb-4aa3-4c9f-9159-a32d157e5f93?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in April 2025 and later passed the expanded SAVE America proposal. As of November 20, those efforts have not produced an enacted federal law requiring documentary proof of citizenship when registering for federal elections. Noncitizen voting is already prohibited; the proposals concern additional verification requirements.
House passage deserves credit. Failure to deliver enactment deserves an accounting.
Republican leadership knew the Senate rules, the opposition, and the election calendar. What was the strategy? When it stalled, what changed? Who was responsible for getting it finished?
On election integrity, voters were promised cattle. They are entitled to ask why so much of what arrived was a hat.
The unfinished legislation does not establish that illegal voting caused Republican losses. It does leave leadership explaining why something it called essential remained undone.
Voters should demand completed investigations, accessible audit findings, and documented reconciliation work. A secret ballot protects how someone voted. It does not relieve officials of the obligation to demonstrate that required procedures were followed.
Voters did not elect Republicans to become well-paid spectators to their own defeat.
They gave you power. You gave them excuses, unfinished promises, and candidates they were expected to support simply because the alternative was worse.
If there was election misconduct, prove it and pursue it. If your candidates and leadership failed, own it. You do not get to use suspicion about the first to escape responsibility for the second.
**The voters are not your emergency fund. Stop sending them the bill for your incompetence.**

Honoring lives lost, protecting lives today, and taking our California work nationwide. | |
Peter, Today, on **Transgender Day of Remembrance** , we honor the transgender people whose lives have been taken by violence. We remember the people behind the names, and the families and communities living with their loss. We recommit ourselves to the work of protecting the people who are still here. **In California, I've fought to make that protection real through legislative action.** I authored the transgender refuge law, which protects young people and families seeking gender-affirming care, strengthened medical privacy protections, and passed legislation to improve health care for transgender, gender-diverse, and intersex people. I also jointly authored the Gender Recognition Act to make it easier to obtain accurate IDs and, as Senate Budget Chair, secured $15 million for gender-affirming health care - which Donald Trump is trying to cut from Medicaid. **These are protections everyone should be able to count on – _no matter what state they live in._** In Congress, I'll fight to pass the Equality Act, protect access to gender-affirming care, and reverse Trump's attacks on transgender people in our military, health care system and schools. body:
New FBI Records Reveal Crooks’ Venmo Account Suspended After Trump
Assassination Attempt

[INSIDE JW]

COURT FOLLOWS JUDICIAL WATCH LEAD ON ILHAN OMAR SEARCH WARRANT
RECORDS!

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=39238&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly95b3V0dS5iZS9GY2lKMTJqMmFSZz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&H=9cd485ed2a3ad5ccd273a4ba4860239f217bfd4049a1a82fdab4f9b9d68a9e0e]

VICTORY: JUDGE ORDERS UNSEALING OF ILHAN OMAR SEARCH WARRANT RECORDS

Chief Judge James E. Boasberg of the U.S. District Court for the
District of Columbia ordered
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=39239&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL29tYXItc2VhcmNoLXdhcnJhbnQtb3JkZXItMDAxNDQvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&H=88e6d5db8be9aab7651e2631feb70d236319c6ad9aa4b521cf73b18fdb488725]
that Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-NY) search warrant records on the sealed
docket be partially released to the public on Monday, November 23.

The order follows a November 17 hearing
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=39197&F=T&&H=f5afb45c9ad80116c5d91f845526d696ef7473ef5560280b05293e4eda04e04b]
in our and media organizations’ requests to unseal the search
warrant and related records (_In re Application of Fourteen Press
Organizations for Access to Sealed Search Warrant Records_, No.
1:26-mc-00144 (D.D.C.)).

The court agreed with us that most of the material could be released
without impairing any criminal investigation
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=39197&F=T&&H=f5afb45c9ad80116c5d91f845526d696ef7473ef5560280b05293e4eda04e04b]
into Omar.

Boasberg ordered
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=39239&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL29tYXItc2VhcmNoLXdhcnJhbnQtb3JkZXItMDAxNDQvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&H=88e6d5db8be9aab7651e2631feb70d236319c6ad9aa4b521cf73b18fdb488725]
the government to submit the records to the court by November 20,
including the search-warrant docket sheet, for review in both redacted
and unredacted forms. The court’s order states:

> 1) By November 20, 2026, the Government shall submit to the Court
> _ex parte_ all documents on the SW docket (excluding the
> search-warrant affidavit, but including the docket sheet) in
> redboxed and redacted forms; 2) Absent a stay, the Court will
> publish the documents in redacted form on its website no earlier
> than 5:00 p.m. on November 23, 2026; 3) By November 23, 2026, the
> Government shall inform the Court _ex parte_ whether the documents
> in No. 26-mc-159 should be treated differently from those on the SW
> docket and, if so, why; 4) Applicants shall file any response to the
> redactions by November 30, 2026; and 5) The Court will not publish
> any redacted material without speaking to the Government first.

This is an important victory for transparency. Now the American people
will be able to see key information about the search warrant on Ilhan
Omar’s home and what laws she is alleged to have violated.

We filed a motion
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=38971&F=T&&H=77a5d7e3d9ca45f4a9729c311ace56433d1afa9c1c08fc429dd78ed0c446b1b1]
on October 15, 2026, asking the court to unseal records related to the
October 12 search of Omar’s home, including the warrant, its
application, supporting affidavits and attachments, any return and
inventory, the docket sheet, and related briefs, motions, orders,
opinions, and transcripts. The request includes records concerning the
scope of the search and the court’s decision to seal the materials.

We noted that our interest in allegations concerning Omar predates the
search. On July 23, 2019, we filed an ethics complaint
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=38931&F=T&&H=a6bc37caac12588e8a4744a0083dc7bff0eaa739a4075c8d33db4f0492676fa7]
to the Office of Congressional Ethics requesting an investigation into
allegations of perjury, immigration fraud, marriage fraud, state and
federal tax fraud, and federal student loan fraud.

We argue that the public has a right to access the warrant records
under both common law and the First Amendment. Our motion states:

> [T]he public’s need for access is substantial. The government has
> searched an elected official’s home and has publicly acknowledged
> an ongoing criminal investigation, even to the point of commenting
> on its conduct. Representative Omar has disputed the government’s
> account and used the search and those comments to solicit campaign
> contributions. News reports based on unnamed sources have added
> accounts of the Court’s restrictions and the government’s
> requests. The public has a legitimate interest in understanding the
> factual basis for the warrant and the government’s exercise of its
> investigative authority....

We have a record of successfully seeking the release of sealed
search-warrant materials in high-profile federal investigations.

In August 2022, we forced the release
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=27949&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvdHJ1bXAtcmFpZC1hZmZpZGF2aXQtcmVsZWFzZWQvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&H=e71093d70271f408382fd0752596e476f94ed9a09d4e8db1470c34506f7fdc59] of a
heavily redacted affidavit
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=27944&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL3VzYS12LXNlYWxlZC1zZWFyY2gtd2FycmFudC1hZmZpZGF2aXQtMDgzMzIvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&H=1d75ad5d812b8af784e9e95b6a589abeb960526b55ad02a15cdb3ff14cc33e24]
used to obtain the search warrant for the unprecedented FBI raid on
former President Donald Trump’s home at Mar-a-Lago. The release
followed a court order
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=27945&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvY291cnQtZ3JhbnRzLWp3LXJlcXVlc3QtdHJ1bXAtYWZmaWRhdml0Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&H=303e6b406ff822727fe6ea69b7a29dc19bea2002b1291752dae3ea06b1e8b00a]
granting our request to unseal the records.

In August 2026, a federal court unsealed the key search warrant
records
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=38778&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvY291cnQtdW5zZWFscy1zZWNyZXQtZmJpLXJlY29yZHMtbWlrZS1saW5kZWxsLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&H=0a5bc7058ab361d3db028efc334b86d5be4403ff47ac83a76788959889937312]
behind the Biden FBI’s September 2022 seizure of Mike Lindell’s
cell phone (_In the Matter of the Search of a Person Located in the
District of Minnesota_ (No. 22-mj-742 (TNL))). The records, unsealed
at the request of Judicial Watch and Mike Lindell, show that the Biden
FBI used private litigant Dominion Voting Systems’ then-pending $1.3
billion defamation lawsuit against Mike Lindell and others (a lawsuit
that had been settled
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=38768&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZm94OS5jb20vbmV3cy9taWtlLWxpbmRlbGwtbXlwaWxsb3ctZG9taW5pb24tbGF3c3VpdC0yMDIwLWVsZWN0aW9uP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&H=e90507c4bcbc6936d115dc722b1cb6a2c320523fcf85d40b55e468febf959c39]
as to Lindell earlier this year) as well as other information from
Dominion as part of its justification for seeking the warrant.

We have also moved to unseal warrant materials targeting Rudy
Giuliani
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=38592&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZ2l1bGlhbmlzLXBob25lLWFuZC1lbWFpbC8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&H=6f5b630377a17a2181606c9362b1ceedd6d0b39499a2d8ee99e94aa7042aa8c1], Victoria
Toensing
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=38448&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZm9ybWVyLXRydW1wLWxhd3llcnMtcGhvbmUtZW1haWwvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&H=88a40d42972e0bad38ce2024e791e2e0f9c3ad5cd221ed622e8ec6116493ea6c],
and Michael Caputo
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=38117&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvbWljaGFlbC1jYXB1dG9zLWdvb2dsZS1hY2NvdW50Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&H=4656a001a512ca3f0dfbfc42674d44bb535db48b0f369aa87370300c3592f6c3].

CIA REFUSES TO CONFIRM OR DENY EXISTENCE OF JANUARY 6 RECORDS

We have to wonder what the CIA is up to.

Instead of producing records concerning the January 6, 2021, events at
the U.S. Capitol, as a court ordered under the Freedom of Information
Act (FOIA), the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), now claims
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=39245&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtY2lhLWo2LW5vdGljZS0wMjE3Mi8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&H=f2cccc5b152c1be6b9d6c3e1f0341edd325f468bdc15523e1d2b2a35c22402e3] it
cannot confirm nor deny whether it has records – a dramatic reversal
after the CIA’s previous acknowledgement that a significant volume
of records had been located.

In October, Judge Jia M. Cobb had ordered
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=38983&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvY291cnQtb3JkZXJzLWNpYS1wcm9kdWNpbmctamFudWFyeS02LXJlY29yZHMvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&H=eff6b4deb43607ad7a70e793b8b91f7d823440996fe99e54dab89b868a9e6e71]
the CIA to begin producing records it said it was reviewing on
November 16. Instead, the CIA claimed in a November 13 letter
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=39245&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtY2lhLWo2LW5vdGljZS0wMjE3Mi8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&H=f2cccc5b152c1be6b9d6c3e1f0341edd325f468bdc15523e1d2b2a35c22402e3]
that it could not “confirm or deny the existence” of any records
related to January 6, 2021:

> [I]n accordance with Section 3.6(a) of Executive Order 13526, as
> amended, the CIA can neither confirm or deny the existence or
> nonexistence of records to your request. The fact of the existence
> or nonexistence of such records is itself currently and properly
> classified and relates to intelligence sources and methods
> information protected from disclosure by Section 102A(h)(l) of the
> National Security Act of 1947, as amended, and Section 6 of the CIA
> Act of 1949, as amended. Therefore, these items of your request are
> denied pursuant to FOIA exemptions (b)(l) and (b)(3).

In a court filing
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=39245&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtY2lhLWo2LW5vdGljZS0wMjE3Mi8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&H=f2cccc5b152c1be6b9d6c3e1f0341edd325f468bdc15523e1d2b2a35c22402e3] we
pointed out that “after previously confirming that a significant
volume of records had been located and even suggesting discussions to
narrow the request,” the CIA “now, for the first time, asserts
that it cannot confirm or deny the existence of records.” We
requested an in-person hearing or a status report earlier than
December 1, 2026, to address the agency’s failure to begin
production of records as ordered.

We filed the July 2024 lawsuit
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=33154&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvamFudWFyeS02LTIwMjEtcHJvdGVzdHMvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&H=70b941b9635c81c8527d29f65f0aa40107d904011daf6c73d7e452ab5793c9f2] after the CIA
failed to respond to a March 2024 FOIA request asking the agency to
produce CIA records concerning the January 6, 2021, events in
Washington, DC, including shots fired and a person shot inside the
U.S. Capitol, requests for CIA assistance, bomb technicians and
bomb-detection dogs deployed or placed on standby, and after-action
reports documenting the events (_Judicial Watch v. Central
Intelligence Agency_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=33131&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtY2lhLWo2LXNob3RzLWJvbWItdGVjaC1jb21wbGFpbnQtMDIxNzIvXV8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&H=b1b0cb6cab1591e913d74298485f551f68f0c5b594d7b431f34289e774d1407f _(No.
1:24-cv-02172)).

In March 2024, we received 88 pages
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=31656&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvY2lhLWJvbWItdGVjaHMtamFudWFyeS02Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&H=66d5cf6bb7d551049160502e5c6af74bce9127e6e95cd12af94adf1405bb076d] of Bureau of
Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) records from the
Department of Justice in a FOIA lawsuit that show the CIA deployed
personnel to Washington, DC on January 6, 2021.

The records include a series of text messages under the heading
“January 7 Intel Chain
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=31595&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLWF0Zi1qYW4tNi1wcm9kLTEtMDE2MDgtcGdzLTQ5LTg4L13igJ0/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&H=98d66bf1a6f2a78a718bdc644294c9fb81ae026f3d17af78db26f680d91480a4

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=39211&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2ZvaWEtYWR2aXNvcnktY210ZS1iZWtlc2hhLTIwMjYvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&H=1c8ba91901d79223ffe10e3f379ce848d8f91f3e0a3e20e2d2236bebc67c710d]

advocates on FOIA matters.

Established in 2014, the FOIA Advisory Committee, under the umbrella
of the Office of Government Information Services at NARA, brings
together representatives of federal agencies and the FOIA requester
community to improve the administration of the Freedom of Information
Act. The committee’s mission includes fostering dialogue between the
federal government and FOIA requesters, soliciting public comments,
and recommending improvements to FOIA administration and proactive
disclosure of government records.

The committee’s seventh term begins in December 2026 in Washington,
DC, when the committee will organize into working subcommittees to
address issues involving FOIA administration and government
transparency.

TSA ALLOWS ‘UNCLEARED INDIVIDUALS’ TO ACCESS CRITICAL AREAS AT
AIRPORTS

The bureaucrats who are paid to protect us are failing us, our
_Corruption Chronicles_ blog reports
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=39216&F=T&&H=7cfba10f7349fbf98b3ed469bb345e7fd14270057c145abac8cebb2a0da24109].

> In a significant lapse decades after the worst terrorist attack on
> American soil, the federal agency created to protect the nation’s
> transportation system compromises national security by failing to
> ensure airport workers have required security clearance. It is
> unthinkable negligence on the part of the Transportation Security
> Administration (TSA), the 65,000-employee conglomerate established
> after 19 Islamist terrorists hijacked four domestic airliners that
> crashed into New York’s World Trade Center, the Pentagon, and
> Stony Creek Township in Pennsylvania. Among TSA’s critical duties
> is conducting thorough background checks on airport workers,
> including store attendants, baggage handlers, and restaurant staff.
> The process includes certifying the identity of applicants, checking
> whether they pose a security threat and confirming legal residency
> in the United States. Once fully vetted, some airport workers get
> badges that provide access to restricted areas where sensitive
> operations occur.
>
> Incredibly, a federal probe
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=39246&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cub2lnLmRocy5nb3Yvc2l0ZXMvZGVmYXVsdC9maWxlcy9hc3NldHMvMjAyNi0xMS9PSUctMjctMDMtTm92MjYtUmVkYWN0ZWQucGRmP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&H=b3beb7d194824cc2302ab3d5c2108fdea7202e0664a52ef29c09f4d5aa35f509]
> released to the public this month reveals that the TSA does not
> adequately ensure airport workers are properly screened before
> obtaining badges that grant access to those secured zones of the
> nation’s airports. This has allowed “uncleared individuals to
> access areas where they could inflict harm,” the investigation,
> conducted by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) inspector
> general found. In some cases, airport workers who provided
> inaccurate Social Security numbers during the application process
> were awarded badges to access restricted portions of an airport. In
> others key biographical data were inconsistent with applicant
> records reviewed by the DHS watchdog. “TSA’s system used for
> assessing workers for threats contained inaccurate and incomplete
> information,” the report states. “We compared the information
> airport operators collected and the information TSA used to conduct
> security threat assessments and found that key biographic data
> points were inconsistent” for what appears to be a substantial
> number of sampled records, though the exact figure is redacted in
> the report along with other big chunks of data. “Without complete
> and accurate information on applicants, TSA risks conducting a
> security threat assessment on the wrong individual and missing
> derogatory information associated with the real applicant.”
>
> The samples were taken during a recent two-year period and though a
> lot of key details are redacted in the public version of the report,
> it is clear the agency repeatedly dropped the ball. For example,
> during the period examined, investigators found that airport
> operators issued badges to workers whose security threat assessments
> were not yet complete and later found to be a threat by TSA, which
> eventually delivered “Do Not Issue” notices. TSA failed to
> discover the blunders in a timely manner because the agency did not
> bother to conduct inspections of airport operations, including the
> status of employee badges, and failed to follow up to ensure badges
> were revoked. In one case, an airport employee was allowed to hold
> an active badge for 177 days before it was rescinded. The agency
> also failed to ensure that airports enrolled employees in a Federal
> Bureau of Investigation (FBI) program called Rap Back that conducts
> recurrent vetting and sends airport operators status notifications
> of any subsequent criminal information changes on enrolled
> individuals. TSA officials provided the DHS IG with the excuse that
> they do not have sufficient resources to “review 100 percent of
> airport operators’ records” to assure compliance with the FBI
> program’s enrollment requirements.
>
> This is the second DHS agency exposed in the last few months for
> failing to properly vet employees in critical positions that could
> compromise national security. A few weeks ago, Judicial
> Watch reported
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86720&L=38904&F=T&&H=76fa9e7da0c5d0cf430e0d177f95638dad3d6f1161da09196af80418efa2b08b]
> that U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), the DHS
> agency that oversees lawful immigration to the United States, allows
> asylum, adjudication, and immigration officers whose national
> security eligibility was denied or revoked to work in sensitive
> positions that require the clearance. This is significant because
> the agency, with around 24,000 employees in hundreds of offices
> worldwide, administers essential programs that permit foreign
> nationals to visit, work, study, live and seek refuge in the
> country. By failing to properly screen employees the agency creates
> a “significant risk” that the officers “could make immigration
> decisions that gravely damage national security or obtain access to
> highly sensitive information,” according to the DHS IG.

[] VICTORY: JUDGE ORDERS UNSEALING OF ILHAN OMAR SEARCH WARRANT RECORDS Chief Judge James E. Boasberg of the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia ordered [] that Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-NY) search warrant records on the sealed docket be partially released to the public on Monday, November 23. The order follows a November 17 hearing [] in our and media organizations’ requests to unseal the search warrant and related records (In re Application of Fourteen Press Organizations for Access to Sealed Search Warrant Records, No. 1:26-mc-00144 (D.D.C.)). The court agreed with us that most of the material could be released without impairing any criminal investigation [] into Omar. Boasberg ordered [] the government to submit the records to the court by November 20, including the search-warrant docket sheet, for review in both redacted and unredacted forms. The court’s order states: 1) By November 20, 2026, the Government shall submit to the Court ex parte all documents on the SW docket (excluding the search-warrant affidavit, but including the docket sheet) in redboxed and redacted forms; 2) Absent a stay, the Court will publish the documents in redacted form on its website no earlier than 5:00 p.m. on November 23, 2026; 3) By November 23, 2026, the Government shall inform the Court ex parte whether the documents in No. 26-mc-159 should be treated differently from those on the SW docket and, if so, why; 4) Applicants shall file any response to the redactions by November 30, 2026; and 5) The Court will not publish any redacted material without speaking to the Government first. This is an important victory for transparency. Now the American people will be able to see key information about the search warrant on Ilhan Omar’s home and what laws she is alleged to have violated. We filed a motion [] on October 15, 2026, asking the court to unseal records related to the October 12 search of Omar’s home, including the warrant, its application, supporting affidavits and attachments, any return and inventory, the docket sheet, and related briefs, motions, orders, opinions, and transcripts. The request includes records concerning the scope of the search and the court’s decision to seal the materials. We noted that our interest in allegations concerning Omar predates the search. On July 23, 2019, we filed an ethics complaint [] to the Office of Congressional Ethics requesting an investigation into allegations of perjury, immigration fraud, marriage fraud, state and federal tax fraud, and federal student loan fraud. We argue that the public has a right to access the warrant records under both common law and the First Amendment. Our motion states: [T]he public’s need for access is substantial. The government has searched an elected official’s home and has publicly acknowledged an ongoing criminal investigation, even to the point of commenting on its conduct. Representative Omar has disputed the government’s account and used the search and those comments to solicit campaign contributions. News reports based on unnamed sources have added accounts of the Court’s restrictions and the government’s requests. The public has a legitimate interest in understanding the factual basis for the warrant and the government’s exercise of its investigative authority.... We have a record of successfully seeking the release of sealed search-warrant materials in high-profile federal investigations. In August 2022, we forced the release [] of a heavily redacted affidavit [] used to obtain the search warrant for the unprecedented FBI raid on former President Donald Trump’s home at Mar-a-Lago. The release followed a court order [] granting our request to unseal the records. In August 2026, a federal court unsealed the key search warrant records [] behind the Biden FBI’s September 2022 seizure of Mike Lindell’s cell phone (In the Matter of the Search of a Person Located in the District of Minnesota (No. 22-mj-742 (TNL))). The records, unsealed at the request of Judicial Watch and Mike Lindell, show that the Biden FBI used private litigant Dominion Voting Systems’ then-pending $1.3 billion defamation lawsuit against Mike Lindell and others (a lawsuit that had been settled [] as to Lindell earlier this year) as well as other information from Dominion as part of its justification for seeking the warrant. We have also moved to unseal warrant materials targeting Rudy Giuliani [], Victoria Toensing [], and Michael Caputo []. CIA REFUSES TO CONFIRM OR DENY EXISTENCE OF JANUARY 6 RECORDS We have to wonder what the CIA is up to. Instead of producing records concerning the January 6, 2021, events at the U.S. Capitol, as a court ordered under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), now claims [] it cannot confirm nor deny whether it has records – a dramatic reversal after the CIA’s previous acknowledgement that a significant volume of records had been located. In October, Judge Jia M. Cobb had ordered [] the CIA to begin producing records it said it was reviewing on November 16. Instead, the CIA claimed in a November 13 letter [] that it could not “confirm or deny the existence” of any records related to January 6, 2021: [I]n accordance with Section 3.6(a) of Executive Order 13526, as amended, the CIA can neither confirm or deny the existence or nonexistence of records to your request. The fact of the existence or nonexistence of such records is itself currently and properly classified and relates to intelligence sources and methods information protected from disclosure by Section 102A(h)(l) of the National Security Act of 1947, as amended, and Section 6 of the CIA Act of 1949, as amended. Therefore, these items of your request are denied pursuant to FOIA exemptions (b)(l) and (b)(3). In a court filing [] we pointed out that “after previously confirming that a significant volume of records had been located and even suggesting discussions to narrow the request,” the CIA “now, for the first time, asserts that it cannot confirm or deny the existence of records.” We requested an in-person hearing or a status report earlier than December 1, 2026, to address the agency’s failure to begin production of records as ordered. We filed the July 2024 lawsuit [] after the CIA failed to respond to a March 2024 FOIA request asking the agency to produce CIA records concerning the January 6, 2021, events in Washington, DC, including shots fired and a person shot inside the U.S. Capitol, requests for CIA assistance, bomb technicians and bomb-detection dogs deployed or placed on standby, and after-action reports documenting the events (Judicial Watch v. Central Intelligence Agency [ (No. 1:24-cv-02172)). In March 2024, we received 88 pages [] of Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) records from the Department of Justice in a FOIA lawsuit that show the CIA deployed personnel to Washington, DC on January 6, 2021. The records include a series of text messages under the heading “January 7 Intel Chain [ in which two separate references to participation by the CIA are made. One states [] that “two CIA bomb techs” are assisting with “a pipe bomb scene on New Jersey and D ST SE.” Another record references “several CIA dog teams on standby [ In an October 15, 2026, minute order [], U.S. District Judge Jia M. Cobb directed the CIA to begin rolling interim productions of responsive records by November 16, rejecting the agency’s refusal to provide records next year. The CIA is playing games with the court and the American people about January 6. After previously acknowledging that a significant volume of records had been located, the agency now claims it cannot confirm or deny their existence. This shell game is a scandal. The American people deserve the truth about what the CIA was doing at the U.S. Capitol on January 6. We have pursued details of January 6 on several fronts. In July 2026, we forced the release [] of over 1,000 hours of Washington, DC, Metropolitan Police Department body-worn camera footage from the January 6, 2021, U.S. Capitol event. In April 2026, we filed [] a (FOIA) lawsuit [] against the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) to obtain records related to possible improper targeting of January 6, 2021, Capitol protesters, their supporters, and related nonprofits. In July 2025, we sued [] the U.S. Department of Justice for records on accelerated January 6 prosecutions after Donald Trump was elected president in November 2024. In June 2025, we obtained [] a $4.975 million settlement [] in the wrongful death lawsuit against the U.S. Government filed on behalf of the family of Ashli Babbitt, the U.S. Air Force veteran who was shot and killed [] inside the U.S. Capitol by then-Capitol Police Lt. Michael Byrd on January 6, 2021. Ashli Babbitt was the only January 6 homicide victim. In October 2023, we received the declaration [] of James W. Joyce, senior counsel in the Office of the General Counsel for the Capitol Police, in which he describes emails among senior officials of the United States Capitol Police (USCP) in January 2021 that show warnings of possible January 6 protests that could lead to serious disruptions at the U.S. Capitol. JUDICIAL WATCH ATTORNEY APPOINTED TO FEDERAL FOIA ADVISORY COMMITTEE Michael Bekesha, our director of constitutional rights litigation, has been reappointed [] by the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) to serve on the 2026-2028 Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Advisory Committee [], representing Judicial Watch and the interests of the FOIA requester community. Bekesha previously served during the 2016-2018 term. Bradford P. Wilson, archivist of the United States, appointed Bekesha to the committee in a November 6, 2026, letter [] that recognizes Judicial Watch as a nongovernmental organization that advocates on FOIA matters. Established in 2014, the FOIA Advisory Committee, under the umbrella of the Office of Government Information Services at NARA, brings together representatives of federal agencies and the FOIA requester community to improve the administration of the Freedom of Information Act. The committee’s mission includes fostering dialogue between the federal government and FOIA requesters, soliciting public comments, and recommending improvements to FOIA administration and proactive disclosure of government records. The committee’s seventh term begins in December 2026 in Washington, DC, when the committee will organize into working subcommittees to address issues involving FOIA administration and government transparency. Judicial Watch [] is one of the nation’s leading public interest organizations dedicated to exposing government corruption and promoting transparency, accountability, and integrity in government. Through FOIA requests and litigation, Judicial Watch has secured the release of millions of pages of government records from federal, state, and local agencies. Bekesha’s reappointment allows us to continue bringing our extensive experience litigating FOIA cases and advocating for the public’s right to know directly to the federal advisory process. The FOIA Advisory Committee operates under the Federal Advisory Committee Act [], as amended (5 U.S.C. §§ 1001-1014). TSA ALLOWS ‘UNCLEARED INDIVIDUALS’ TO ACCESS CRITICAL AREAS AT AIRPORTS The bureaucrats who are paid to protect us are failing us, our Corruption Chronicles_ blog reports []. In a significant lapse decades after the worst terrorist attack on American soil, the federal agency created to protect the nation’s transportation system compromises national security by failing to ensure airport workers have required security clearance. It is unthinkable negligence on the part of the Transportation Security Administration (TSA), the 65,000-employee conglomerate established after 19 Islamist terrorists hijacked four domestic airliners that crashed into New York’s World Trade Center, the Pentagon, and Stony Creek Township in Pennsylvania. Among TSA’s critical duties is conducting thorough background checks on airport workers, including store attendants, baggage handlers, and restaurant staff. The process includes certifying the identity of applicants, checking whether they pose a security threat and confirming legal residency in the United States. Once fully vetted, some airport workers get badges that provide access to restricted areas where sensitive operations occur. Incredibly, a federal probe [] released to the public this month reveals that the TSA does not adequately ensure airport workers are properly screened before obtaining badges that grant access to those secured zones of the nation’s airports. This has allowed “uncleared individuals to access areas where they could inflict harm,” the investigation, conducted by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) inspector general found. In some cases, airport workers who provided inaccurate Social Security numbers during the application process were awarded badges to access restricted portions of an airport. In others key biographical data were inconsistent with applicant records reviewed by the DHS watchdog. “TSA’s system used for assessing workers for threats contained inaccurate and incomplete information,” the report states. “We compared the information airport operators collected and the information TSA used to conduct security threat assessments and found that key biographic data points were inconsistent” for what appears to be a substantial number of sampled records, though the exact figure is redacted in the report along with other big chunks of data. “Without complete and accurate information on applicants, TSA risks conducting a security threat assessment on the wrong individual and missing derogatory information associated with the real applicant.” The samples were taken during a recent two-year period and though a lot of key details are redacted in the public version of the report, it is clear the agency repeatedly dropped the ball. For example, during the period examined, investigators found that airport operators issued badges to workers whose security threat assessments were not yet complete and later found to be a threat by TSA, which eventually delivered “Do Not Issue” notices. TSA failed to discover the blunders in a timely manner because the agency did not bother to conduct inspections of airport operations, including the status of employee badges, and failed to follow up to ensure badges were revoked. In one case, an airport employee was allowed to hold an active badge for 177 days before it was rescinded. The agency also failed to ensure that airports enrolled employees in a Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) program called Rap Back that conducts recurrent vetting and sends airport operators status notifications of any subsequent criminal information changes on enrolled individuals. TSA officials provided the DHS IG with the excuse that they do not have sufficient resources to “review 100 percent of airport operators’ records” to assure compliance with the FBI program’s enrollment requirements. This is the second DHS agency exposed in the last few months for failing to properly vet employees in critical positions that could compromise national security. A few weeks ago, Judicial Watch reported [] that U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), the DHS agency that oversees lawful immigration to the United States, allows asylum, adjudication, and immigration officers whose national security eligibility was denied or revoked to work in sensitive positions that require the clearance. This is significant because the agency, with around 24,000 employees in hundreds of offices worldwide, administers essential programs that permit foreign nationals to visit, work, study, live and seek refuge in the country. By failing to properly screen employees the agency creates a “significant risk” that the officers “could make immigration decisions that gravely damage national security or obtain access to highly sensitive information,” according to the DHS IG. subject: Please contribute to provide turkeys to families who need help this Thanksgiving.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
In these trying times, it is vital that we come together in community to care for one another. We can be the bridge to the society we want to become.
#
Every year, we team up with NYC public housing developments, community organizations, houses of worship, food pantries and local elected officials to give hundreds of families turkeys for their Thanksgiving tables.
This year, we have a goal of donating 1,200 turkeys at 31 events all across my Congressional District.
We’ve run the numbers, and around $30 means a family without a turkey gets to share in the Thanksgiving season at the same time many of us are enjoying a meal surrounded by those we love.
If you'd like to help cover the cost of providing a Thanksgiving meal to a family in my district, it’d mean a lot to share the word that people from all across New York and the country made this possible. Every single dollar we raise will go right toward this program.
[Please make a contribution of $15, $30 or whatever you can afford to help fund our fundraising drive to provide Thanksgiving meals to families who need it in my district. ](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-turkey-26.9SErSW&refcode=em20261121-12516-P_FND_EXP_MIS&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=12516%2E2526796%2EJI5eaP)

By the grace of God, I'm deeply grateful to have won a tough midterm race that included some of the nastiest and most outlandish attacks I've seen in politics. The saddest part was knowing my dad had to watch those terrible commercials about his son in his final weeks.
Several Democrats on the House floor told me they were surprised I won because we were heavily outspent and they threw everything they had at us. It was a hard fight from start to finish, and we left nothing on the table.
Thank you again to everyone who helped. It is an honor to earn your trust to represent the best district in America for a second term.
This weekend I'm finally getting some downtime and catching up on the honey-do list; time on the tractor, the chainsaw, fixing the driveway, and a bunch of other yard work.
I'm fired up and getting after it. Hope to see you around the district soon.

---
This week, I sent a formal letter to House Oversight Chairman James Comer requesting a full congressional oversight hearing into the ongoing failures at Albemarle County Public Schools.
If I were a parent with a child in Albemarle County right now, I would be deeply concerned for their safety. Constituents across the political spectrum have reached out to my office demanding action. The children harmed by these crimes matter deeply to families across our community. It is time to put politics aside, focus on the kids, and demand real accountability.
Albemarle County Public Schools has a clear and dangerous pattern of failing to protect children: (These individuals are presumed innocent until proven guilty.)
• First, former Hollymead Elementary staffer Michael Swiney was indicted on 20 felony counts involving the sexual abuse of multiple students. A major part of that scandal was the nearly six-month delay between the start of the investigation in January and when parents and the School Board were finally notified in June. That failure led to the resignation of Superintendent Matthew Haas, the removal of Hollymead's principal, and criminal charges against three administrators for failing to report suspected abuse.
• Next, former Woodbrook Elementary teacher Nicholas Clark was arrested for child pornography and later pleaded guilty to five felony counts of possession.
• Now we have learned that 524 employees hired over the past three years were never properly screened against Virginia's Child Protective Services Central Registry for founded complaints of child abuse or neglect, forcing the division to close schools ahead of Thanksgiving break.
I was the first elected official to formally call for an independent investigation. On July 9, I wrote to Governor Abigail Spanberger and Attorney General Jay Jones demanding a full-scale, independent third-party state investigation. That call quickly drew bipartisan support. On July 18, three Democratic state lawmakers, Sen. Creigh Deeds, Del. Katrina Callsen, and Del. Amy Laufer, sent their own letter to the Albemarle County School Board urging an independent investigation. Governor Spanberger followed with her own call for an investigation shortly thereafter.
These are not isolated mistakes. They are a repeated failure to put the safety of kids first. Parents deserve better. Children deserve better. Enough is enough.
I also wrote to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent seeking answers on Governor Spanberger's decision to block Virginia's participation in the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit (also known as the Education Freedom Tax Credit) for 2027. Under this program, taxpayers can claim a dollar-for-dollar federal tax credit of up to $1,700 per individual (or $3,400 for married couples filing jointly) for donations to approved Scholarship-Granting Organizations. Those scholarships can help pay for tutoring, special-needs services, textbooks, and tuition at both public and private schools.
By refusing to submit Virginia's list of eligible organizations, Governor Spanberger is denying Virginia families access to these resources starting in 2027. Parents in Albemarle County are looking for safer options for their children right now. Her decision makes it harder for them to find those options. I'm calling on Governor Spanberger to reverse course and allow Virginia parents to access these federal tax credits.
Protecting our children is not a Republican or Democrat issue, it should be a number one issue. I will keep fighting until the adults in charge do their jobs and keep our kids safe.
Quick Note on Recent Attacks:
Political operatives falsely claim that I "support child marriage" because I (at the time a State Senator) and 42 House of Delegate Members voted against a 2024 bill (HB 994) that raised Virginia's marriage age to 18 with no exceptions. Prior to that bill, 16- and 17-year-olds could only marry if a judge granted them legal emancipation and approval. A 17-year-old can enlist in the military, deploy, and risk their life for this country. I didn't want to remove the narrow judicial emancipation option that would allow a young service member's spouse and child to receive full military survivor benefits if they died in combat. Opposing a bill over a narrow exception for military families is not supporting child marriage, it is a deliberate distortion meant to distract from real failures like those in Albemarle County.
Additionally, on November 18, 2025, I voted with nearly the entire House (427-1) to pass the Epstein Files Transparency Act to release all Epstein files. Earlier this year, I even traveled to Chappaqua, New York, to be one of only a handful of lawmakers in history to question a former president and former secretary of state, Bill and Hillary Clinton, under oath as part of the House Oversight Committee's Epstein investigation.
On a brighter note, I was honored to attend a ceremony celebrating the 251st Birthday of the U.S. Marine Corps with a cake cutting, spoke with Vulcan Industries, and gave remarks to The Virginia Chamber of Commerce on Capitol Hill.
Overall, it was a light legislative week, with roughly a dozen bills advanced and four recorded votes before the House departed for the Thanksgiving district work period.
When we return, it is my hope we can work as a team, prevent a government shutdown, pass the Farm Bill, pass the NDAA, confirm judges, and more.
