clean_body: | | | == == The Honey Do List | By the grace of God, I'm deeply grateful to have won a tough midterm race that included some of the nastiest and most outlandish attacks I've seen in politics. The saddest part was knowing my dad had to watch those terrible commercials about his son in his final weeks. Several Democrats on the House floor told me they were surprised I won because we were heavily outspent and they threw everything they had at us. It was a hard fight from start to finish, and we left nothing on the table. Thank you again to everyone who helped. It is an honor to earn your trust to represent the best district in America for a second term. This weekend I'm finally getting some downtime and catching up on the honey-do list; time on the tractor, the chainsaw, fixing the driveway, and a bunch of other yard work. I'm fired up and getting after it. Hope to see you around the district soon. Weekly Recap - Protecting Virginia's Children | == This week, I sent a formal letter to House Oversight Chairman James Comer requesting a full congressional oversight hearing into the ongoing failures at Albemarle County Public Schools. If I were a parent with a child in Albemarle County right now, I would be deeply concerned for their safety. Constituents across the political spectrum have reached out to my office demanding action. The children harmed by these crimes matter deeply to families across our community. It is time to put politics aside, focus on the kids, and demand real accountability. Albemarle County Public Schools has a clear and dangerous pattern of failing to protect children: (These individuals are presumed innocent until proven guilty.) • First, former Hollymead Elementary staffer Michael Swiney was indicted on 20 felony counts involving the sexual abuse of multiple students. A major part of that scandal was the nearly six-month delay between the start of the investigation in January and when parents and the School Board were finally notified in June. That failure led to the resignation of Superintendent Matthew Haas, the removal of Hollymead's principal, and criminal charges against three administrators for failing to report suspected abuse. • Next, former Woodbrook Elementary teacher Nicholas Clark was arrested for child pornography and later pleaded guilty to five felony counts of possession. • Now we have learned that 524 employees hired over the past three years were never properly screened against Virginia's Child Protective Services Central Registry for founded complaints of child abuse or neglect, forcing the division to close schools ahead of Thanksgiving break. I was the first elected official to formally call for an independent investigation. On July 9, I wrote to Governor Abigail Spanberger and Attorney General Jay Jones demanding a full-scale, independent third-party state investigation. That call quickly drew bipartisan support. On July 18, three Democratic state lawmakers, Sen. Creigh Deeds, Del. Katrina Callsen, and Del. Amy Laufer, sent their own letter to the Albemarle County School Board urging an independent investigation. Governor Spanberger followed with her own call for an investigation shortly thereafter. These are not isolated mistakes. They are a repeated failure to put the safety of kids first. Parents deserve better. Children deserve better. Enough is enough. I also wrote to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent seeking answers on Governor Spanberger's decision to block Virginia's participation in the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit (also known as the Education Freedom Tax Credit) for 2027. Under this program, taxpayers can claim a dollar-for-dollar federal tax credit of up to $1,700 per individual (or $3,400 for married couples filing jointly) for donations to approved Scholarship-Granting Organizations. Those scholarships can help pay for tutoring, special-needs services, textbooks, and tuition at both public and private schools. By refusing to submit Virginia's list of eligible organizations, Governor Spanberger is denying Virginia families access to these resources starting in 2027. Parents in Albemarle County are looking for safer options for their children right now. Her decision makes it harder for them to find those options. I'm calling on Governor Spanberger to reverse course and allow Virginia parents to access these federal tax credits. Protecting our children is not a Republican or Democrat issue, it should be a number one issue. I will keep fighting until the adults in charge do their jobs and keep our kids safe. Quick Note on Recent Attacks: Political operatives falsely claim that I "support child marriage" because I (at the time a State Senator) and 42 House of Delegate Members voted against a 2024 bill (HB 994) that raised Virginia's marriage age to 18 with no exceptions. Prior to that bill, 16- and 17-year-olds could only marry if a judge granted them legal emancipation and approval. A 17-year-old can enlist in the military, deploy, and risk their life for this country. I didn't want to remove the narrow judicial emancipation option that would allow a young service member's spouse and child to receive full military survivor benefits if they died in combat. Opposing a bill over a narrow exception for military families is not supporting child marriage, it is a deliberate distortion meant to distract from real failures like those in Albemarle County. Additionally, on November 18, 2025, I voted with nearly the entire House (427-1) to pass the Epstein Files Transparency Act to release all Epstein files. Earlier this year, I even traveled to Chappaqua, New York, to be one of only a handful of lawmakers in history to question a former president and former secretary of state, Bill and Hillary Clinton, under oath as part of the House Oversight Committee's Epstein investigation. On a brighter note, I was honored to attend a ceremony celebrating the 251st Birthday of the U.S. Marine Corps with a cake cutting, spoke with Vulcan Industries, and gave remarks to The Virginia Chamber of Commerce on Capitol Hill. Overall, it was a light legislative week, with roughly a dozen bills advanced and four recorded votes before the House departed for the Thanksgiving district work period. When we return, it is my hope we can work as a team, prevent a government shutdown, pass the Farm Bill, pass the NDAA, confirm judges, and more. Possible Cyber Attacks? | == My team and I have been asking questions about recent tech outages around the country and are being told it is part of an effort to stop or eliminate vulnerabilities from aging infrastructure. President Trump stated that the breakdowns, which have impacted organizations ranging from JPMorgan Chase and Microsoft to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and the National Security Agency (NSA), are "all separate events" and "individual events." Addressing reports of some Americans stockpiling food and water, he told Fox News, "Tell them to relax. Everything's good... I'll let you know if there's a problem." You're Invited! A Christmas Thank You Party - December 19th | == Tracy and I would like to invite you to a special Christmas Thank You Party on Saturday, December 19th, in Appomattox. Let's come together, celebrate the birth of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, and enjoy some fellowship as we recognize the people who made this victory possible! ### **How will 2028 Differ from 2024 and 2026 efforts?**
**Ranked Choice Voting is so popular in Alaska that it took nearly $7 million of 99%+ out-of-state money just to squeak it through in 2020.** **It was so popular in 2024 that it needed ~$15 million (again, ~99% out-of-state) to barely survive a repeal.** **It was so popular in 2026 that it needed another ~$10 million (still overwhelmingly out-of-state) to defend the system.** **That’s $32 million+ of mostly Outside money poured into keeping Ranked Choice Voting alive in Alaska — plus the $50k settlement from the 2025 legal fight against my repeal effort.** **Get ready for another $15 million in 2028. They’ll need it. This time we will break the petitions into two parts.** **—————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————** **The original bill 19AKBE was three parts, it was campaign finance rules (Stop Dark Money), it was Jungle Primary (Open Primary), and it was Ranked Choice Voting (RCV).** **The 2024 Effort (My Effort) Noticed the Campaign Finance Language as a Poison Pill, so I removed it from the Repeal Attempt, they ran ads saying we were trying to give power back to the polticial parties, which was effective, the graphic above shows the result, very close loss even though we were winning for 2 weeks after election day and had a 4,000 vote lead on election day.** **The 2026 Effort (Establishment GOP) tried to repeal the whole 19AKBE and failed very badly even though they raised significantly more money than I did.** **The new Effort targeting 2028 will break the Open Primary and RCV into two bills and run them at the same time in simple language, easily translated, no campaign finance language included.**

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNjcsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABEAa7upoHI3fgsEH-m4P82I6nql81zhhSdWUY-x1nzgJDtcNAoSlp1Lub9-wUMuhwTQXd7d3GZjqTiJT4CmK6aLr8r4dOaWdCD0SNEjH

God’s Children Are Not For Sale

Friend,

Have you ever heard a sound you just couldn’t ignore?

For one woman staying in a hotel, it was the scream of a little girl on the other side of the wall.

I want to introduce you to “Daisy.”

But that’s not her real name. We’ll call her Daisy to protect her privacy.

And her story is why I am writing to you today.

My name is Eduardo Verástegui. I am the producer of the film Sound of Freedom and the new movie Zero A.D.: The Birth of Christ, which hits theaters in December.

Years ago, I met rescuers who told me what really happens to children who are trafficked.

It broke my heart.

And it left me with a question I still can’t shake…

What if it were my child?

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNjcsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABEAa7uppZLzKjCg1eBjEs166USr_8CXiO4SFGtj6tSrJUi4lK-isFbkQqtm0ehNbE9X-PepDddFjlg8rGeTpkefHNDlztUQKwv3SYARJ
Rescue a Child — Give Now

Hollywood said Sound of Freedom would never succeed.

Doors closed. Studios walked away.

But we refused to give up.

Because God’s children are not for sale.

After the film, I started Sound of Freedom Foundation to keep that fight going, long after the credits roll.

Let me show you what that fight looks like.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNjcsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABEAa7upq8fhyl5TrphBt7BTGQljlytxb7GXv6c1WRjPWat_KwcJsa4t-BMYE1dPaXFtGwziMo4eFsrqchET06ACpkINOT9bccJ1iWbMy

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNjcsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABEAa7upr8AwhXwzBWi3byCExLeLqfmyysgi-7iAzMijdf6Nu6hDXqBaQASaqHBjbIhZzjG1qNIrlUbxpGfEWNiJKwaU58NBTxgeT8oH0
Rescue a Child — Give Now

Daisy was only ten years old when her own older sister sold her to a trafficker.

She was forced into a taxi and taken to a hotel, where a grown man was waiting to hurt her.

But Daisy fought back. She screamed as loud as she could.

And the woman next door heard her.

She tried to get inside. When she couldn’t, she ran to the front desk and demanded they call for help.

Police came. The man was arrested.

And Daisy was brought straight to one of our safe children’s homes.

Friend, rescue is only the beginning.

Daisy came to us with wounds no child should ever carry.

For the next couple of years, she was surrounded by safety, love, counseling, and school.

And by people who reminded her every day:

What happened to you does not define you. You are valuable. You are loved. You are God’s child.

Then came the best day of all.

Daisy was placed with her forever family. Today, she is a beloved daughter with a safe home and a bright future.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNjcsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABEAa7upsJmfEOiIof9ykkTPv4-HzrI-w10GXV5LQ4-sFpyESclHpGcXl3-JpEnFczMfeu4gNlOB7hV7cE5p5eqvH1AjGMFrhQ-SArTfL

That is what Sound of Freedom Foundation does.

Rescue. Restore. Raise.

- We help rescue children by equipping the brave agents and partners who find them.
- We restore survivors with a safe place to heal — body, mind, and soul.
- We help raise them in loving families, so they can grow up free.

And we work to stop trafficking before it starts, by helping struggling families and teaching parents the warning signs.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNjcsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABEAa7uptPaE30lyMms4sFvlugZgBgIGqiwB0nvQj9gwaa_U4VjouljI89bMwyOcoa0QI3sN6GSxfLcTmQCnVjaJPAkHtHLJqtwA_jSpL
Rescue a Child — Give Now

Jesus said, “Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.” (Matthew 19:14, NIV)

Every child is precious to God. And I believe He calls us to protect them.

Here is the hard truth, Friend ...

Human trafficking cases have been reported in all 50 U.S. states. And tonight, another child is crying out behind a locked door.

The woman next door could not open that door by herself. But she made sure help came.

You can do the same thing today.

Will you make your first gift to Sound of Freedom Foundation?

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNjcsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABEAa7upuNl_Yox-WPD8ZPrbOnklmd--S5kl_8eeoU4J8tmdXF1qephfwGzPzrENY2q9tXpzeGMzHe2yMjcqzQOd6N74O7YesI3sIjRx9
Will you give $25, $50, $75, $100, or whatever you can right now to help rescue, restore, and raise more children like Daisy?

Your gift helps rescue children from trafficking, restore them with love and healing, and give them the chance to grow up in a safe, loving family.

I often say… when good people keep quiet, they become part of the problem.

Please don’t stay quiet.

Join us today.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNjcsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABEAa7upv5UV_5UqulNg_EJyZHLjeq0kyumZd6_vHevR69rjSUUx2ON-iXm4Fh_RDftPK07m2sEr8UeS8ZvbJb1VXhIQSVU1lvnEYVuhc
Rescue a Child — Give Now

God’s children are not for sale.

With gratitude and prayer,

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNjcsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABEAa7upwCRjmOc_kHkZVuWrgwJE_ReVc9irNhmNqQpQvN7uNXV7lwSfXPlIKeyMiqhLaumpcbIUQy-fcfD44pOAc1hhsUQxAkNXPfk7z

Eduardo Verástegui
Sound of Freedom, Producer
For Sound of Freedom Foundation

P.S. Daisy screamed. A woman listened. Help came. And today, she is safe. Please give now so the next child’s cry is heard, too.

## Coastal Storm Brings Weekend Rain
A coastal storm churning up from the Bahamas is expected to hit the North Carolina coast this weekend with [wind gusts over 50 mph and 2 inches or more of rain](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkD2u3CAUhVeDO0ZwGYMpKNK4e2lTWhiux-hhsOBmrLf7yLOFdEc6Oj_6_nwtXz7lVF6__YFuK2EpePWMRNiWUH0nnzvVdqyYc6glYMQeFhCguZQc5HK22k8MtMghOmOUtnFAJ40dYbRKmmF3erRa6TVqCzCZKVqxqWDFtFnt9SrGIbm7UEqQUopJmYeHVT3VuMIGo5iMZ0-BMVFtjy3_1De2UhvtwbeaU_GPUI8hu53o7Ez9YjAzmK_relwrvW-TwXwPMJil_GgGc_Op8LD7lisR8hVDPVJ58aM25Dl9Y_7htKfOL8RvLJH7I0X-twRsdEe32jD4Tgzmobl4Xinn1LVhT_E6fMqfU_S_SN8O_gUAAP__PumLvw). The National Hurricane Center gave the system a [60% chance of tropical development](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkL0OpCAUhZ8GOyZyUdGCYhu72XZLg9fLSHIFA2TIvv3Gzb7BNqc6OT_fr_f2doFD_Px0F1kfcYvUClOtlDdMrlTHpaZ87cSMKSIdVHCDHiaplAS13TmVm7BuqjusMXpajo6sMssI46KV6U47GZrQTE4778locyjS6Ge_D3oGWlwX7BOoFCil-lmbl4NdD3rcwcPYz8aJoacj1JRfnn-nL-WYcj3R5cQhuhemq2N71noXoX8IWAWsrbVXQ9zxdJlTrfS4BKxPk4BVqUcWAWs8UTZX8QzxI_9dlpya9CnLO5USdiZZc7oDOpYHfYnTfVGsAtYu2-NugTmUyYih_1wu8N899X9pfi38CQAA__9OMIt9) as of Thursday. If it earns a name, it'll be Kyle. Along the Cape Fear coast, rain and storms should [build through Saturday and peak overnight into early Sunday](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkL3u3CAQxJ8Gd1js-gO7oEjj7tKmtDBen9FhsGB1KG8f3Slv8O9GGmlmfvPnsT6sDz4-f9uLzBHdGqmWQMyUV5dsYRsKp3xtFIJL0dFOxa2ocJQAEmG9cyo3OV6h2Y3W3TjvDRnQ84DD3IFuTuNGpcZj6rdunDZldY-z2lUPQDBP86Qbbz6BAAgAaup0a3Hr-m7Y8MBBTdqKXtHuOeX2CH_Tm3JMmU9ncwo-2talqwnmZL6L6H4JXAQutda2kuOPKXD5FAhcAL5a4HL4XFjaQJnlkTI5W1hWohfFXf4nl190yfbl41OW094kcGmy2e_qQ_Bl1KJXz8v68N3AP33wbfBfAAAA__-xCYTp). Bigger waves will reach the southern beaches first, then the Outer Banks, bringing [rip currents, beach erosion, and tidal flooding](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJyk0LGupCAYBeCnwQ7j_4OiBcU2drPtlgbhdySDYIAd77z9zUxyn-DWJ9_Jyfl3W27GBx_vf81Beot2iXSVQLVSXmwypZpQasrHSiHYFC05KnbBDgcOwBGWM6dykq0LNE4rJYbJNaRBTT32kwDV7HrbehjHVUBvnSMzIIhOiq23bkUxgGm8fhcCIAB0o1CtwVVI0a-4Yd-NyjDZkfM15XYLr_SkHFOuuzU5BR9Na9PRBL3XehYm_jCcGc7XdbXXl_eA75jhbHL1NhDD-YP5j-YrGbvzxysQz8ZHnv3Jd3_fefmfN34RPSg6hrOSUuEkZZO1Oy8fgi-DYrK7H8aHz4b62wefGr8DAAD__5lBhoc). ## Drought Reaches 6.2M North Carolinians
More than half of North Carolina's population, 6.2 million people, now [lives in drought-affected areas](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJyk0LHO4yAQBOCnwR0Ru9g4LiiucZdrr7QwbGIkzCIgie7tT75X-OvRNxrNn8f2cDHF_PrtTrLP7LdM35aod6qbZ9e6S61zPXdKyXP2FKj5DRUaCSARtlK5FfJ9gyHYedZmCQNZmJcJp0XDPBw2uH0PQEabhZxB8BpRIwHBokY3uSHaqxAAAUDd9XxzuOtRTzs-cVL32YlRUYid6-2Z_vKHaubaD-8qp5jdzfM5JHv0XprQvwSuAle3e4ArEbgWbl3gmr0Mld-vo8tKzh_UpEF5xpQiZ1mISyJZqVH9cKxNes495jddqghcUanJTHgXuA7VhvK9ZDOzGNXrdDH939F_-uLH4r8AAAD__1sTh2U), according to the state's latest drought report. The Drought Management Advisory Council put [39 central and eastern counties in extreme drought](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJyk0D2OpDAUBODTQGbkH8xP4GATstl0Q_SwH2DJ2Mh-gzW3X3WrbzBxqT6V6t_X-gU--Hj8hQvNHu0asZaARJhXm6AQhEIpXxuGYFO06LDYVXI5MCGYFOudU7nR0ipaZ8ZRDbNr0Yhx1lLPSoztaSxKpye9bfOwa1B6UDC7Cfph4qqfOW-9eYFCSCEEn9TYgdxUr_Qmd6n5NELTc3SeUu728JMezDFlOi3kFHyEzqarDeYkukuj_jRyaeRSa-1qhR961Ctv5HJ8iqwQ-sgw2vSd4cDC3hr7cB5iYZSYTbFgfpBVIMwMCnM5fR8nMYd4YyyNXNps3F19CL4MY9Pz4wIf3nPot2c-Rv4PAAD__7VhjUo) Thursday, with 17 more in severe drought. Durham had 76 days of easily accessible water left as of Nov. 17. Little River Reservoir, one of Durham's main water sources, sits more than 20 feet below full. Falls Lake is 6.57 feet below normal, and Kerr Reservoir is down 9.8 feet. Gov. Josh Stein urged residents to conserve water. _"Unfortunately, only increased rainfall will bring an end to the drought,"_ he said. Klaus Albertin, who chairs the drought council, said the state is roughly 15 inches behind on rain. One wet weekend, he said, won't close that gap.
## Concord's Tree Lighting Returns after Tragedy
Concord's Christmas tree lighting returned to downtown Friday night, one year after gunfire [sent thousands running and left four teenagers wounded](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkM_q2zAQhJ9GvilYK8tyDjqUFtM_pPRXQlt6MRt5HQtkKUjbmLx9cV-h1xkYvm9-XqYLhhjS_Stu5Jbkp0R7jcRMZfIZK2OsnMt2oxh9Tp5mqn6CFnqplAQ1PUquD_I8qWZ21ur-PDfklD0bMGetbLM6xLa1N03LGWEwwwA9dhpag53W3pq-Ce4YVAqUUu2g7QnhpjttbrCAaQeLomtpDpzLaYmv_KSScuHVY8kxJDz5vDXRrcyPKvQ7AaOAcd_3016z5-dRCxgPMQFjzB6jgPGQyWWWIflCWKnKSv5PCfySfi2h8oZVciGSMdxXDukulXwRFokLU5F1zflIBYyfLlYDfPz-7ff4wXzWv96_wY83e71-OVCa4ubHHmIMtbeia-8bhviPmP_376eDvwEAAP__udKWAg). Police Chief Jimmy Hughes promised a larger police presence than in years past, with officers "both seen and unseen." Police blocked off several blocks of downtown hours before the event. Hughes said two groups of teens [opened fire on each other](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkL-OvCAQx58GO4wDKmtB8Wvs9tdeaQYclRyCAXbNvv2Fe4VrJpl8MvP98_Vcnui8C_t_PElvwS6B7uypFEqLjZgL-lxiOg15b2OwtFK2i-jEyAG4gOVKMV9kywLNqpWS47Q2pEFNgxgmCao5tKJNAUp4jBOQMb0ZOwtWqmmQPXaGGqfrQwABAN1DqhaFkb0cjNjE0D0Usr6j1ZWY2s1_4ptSiKkcFlP0LmBr49l4fZRyZSb_MTEzMd_33d6mvCtkYq4CTMwAdUyVYw6F79GFnZtE-M1fmdeEMa3cE66U6n6er-DKh1-JLkzEMYQXel4SEfduP0q9t5TojOHDxNwkvV63897lUbG-2090_tdg-Wu9by1-AgAA___gR5El) just before last year's lighting. Police arrested three teens. Angel Atilano, who owns Charros Mexican Restaurant downtown, pulled fleeing families inside that night. _"It wasn't going to break us as a community,"_ he told WBTV. The city's Christmas parade steps off downtown at 2:30 p.m. today.

## New Push To Cap Property Taxes
Deputy House Speaker Jason Zachary, R-Knoxville, [filed a bill Thursday](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2uozAQBeCnMZ0jbDA_hYtt6LLtlmiwx8TaASx7kpC3v-JK9wluPZqj851_9_kOkeK-_oUNLXOYd3wXQmbMc8pHwswfhtNBeu4e85qP5-5nXetOKiW1msFxfOHcQuXtotUIravQqn402oxN01UP22Ln696Pg2n6Pphx6VwIpmm60NXeD6aK9gpUSiul6sGY2_XqAZ3T_dC0yyDaGn3kI9_4gYz7jqUgBvocL8w3d2wV2QdzKqL5I_Qk9BSOU_XXRejpIgk90eGAhJ4KA6MkeG_wH7MMkbDIH6tkOKWDJJdIJKHIS5xkIvQrFlniKUNcnxmlgy1BXPcqW5_ekSiWrhdtvW4Q6bsT_3LQl9VfAQAA__9py44m) that would limit annual growth in local property tax revenue to inflation plus 2%, unless voters approve more. House Bill 12 would allow unused increases to carry over for four years. Zachary's office says Tennessee is [one of only four states with no property tax limits](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkLtugzAUhp_GbEb42OYyeGgroS5pl0iVuqCDOQGrjo2ME5K3r-grdPmn_6bv6zSc0HkX5g-8ksn5MgTaN085UxrWFFdK-ZnxYXG9hYnSnOItTANUUHMhOIgBbXZ3GhQWkxlBdKhsQUY0nQbdSVkXi2lAadkJVctON_VF2WmstBxraNqubUcqnDkKhQAhRNVqXR7RCclaaFqpxpapiiaXYyrzQplCoG0juvhnvFMqbbwW3iw5rxuTLwx6Bv2-76VdMGcMMc4YDhOD_thh0AtxSMeg11BLDQz6b7QLpifvnaeNvzrv-TnyN1z5eSH-7n6If4YSt_VRJDOtu_PebXXDVDVf0fm_E_mfBO8GfgMAAP__waKCzg). Americans for Prosperity-Tennessee [plans to spend "multiple six figures"](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkL9utDAQxJ8GOp-wDRwULr6G7r42JVrsNVhZjGXv_Xv7iCh5grSjmdH85uM23yBQiOt_2NEw-znisxAyY55TPhJmfjO8LKR7dJjXfNyjm1WjeiGlUHIGy-GBcwu1M4uSI7S2RiOvY6e6Ueu-3syI2o9aOQm9W1w39M0AftCLbe2gG7_UwZyFUiopZTN03eWMOkBr1XXQ7TJUbYMu8JEvvCFjjFgKoqf38cB8scdek9mYU6n0v0pNlZpODLtBjEjjafiRKjXRYYEqNRUGRkHw3OETs_CBsIhfZMHwEhaSWAKRgCJO8CQSoVuxiBJewof1nlFY2BOENdbZuPQMRKH016pt1h0CfU_jP_76MOorAAD__1AukbU) canvassing districts where lawmakers may oppose the measure. _"We 're going to get this passed,"_ said the group's Michael Lotfi. A similar bill stalled in committee earlier this year after the [Tennessee Municipal League](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2O5CAQxfHT4AwLyp8dEGzibDbd0CpDtY0WA6Joe_r2q-kr7AHeT0__P1_rF_rg4_4bTzK1PtdINweqlcqaS8pU6rvit8X8io7KXtIruhUUjFJrCXpFW_1Fa4-NMxvoB_a2IaOnxwDDo-vG5jDPYQYYSc1AatRTp2bVu2HQbiTdOd013vyAWoPWWs3D0P5MHZK1MM1dv82iV-R8TaWtB1WKkZiJnuGdLiqtTWcTzFFrZtH9ErAIWO4cYpvKLmDJiauABVlG5OPyIZDcXuw_CEtHtrxl8ezjLit-y82HwDLgfeJfKixtiuwdFYnSYpYpSh9tIWRiAUtTjMu3D8HzOIle7Sf68LlU_7PnZeBfAAAA__9Q541U) and county leaders testified against it. The league warned that caps could threaten funding for schools, public safety, and infrastructure, particularly in small towns.
## Black Hawks Join Greene County Wildfire Fight
Two Tennessee National Guard Black Hawk helicopters [dumped more than 20,500 gallons of water](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uwyAYRZ_G3ogA47-BoYu3dO1ofYZrB5VghL84zdtX6St0vrrnSOfrOl8pxJC2T7rDMq9zwvOIYEaZc9kzCr-YfhzlR_IoW9kfyc9a6k4oJbSayXE4MRuqvV20Gsm4Glb1Y6vbsWm6-maNB3VqlbqHGdSyKJh1kav0UgNtP9bBvoFKaaWUHNr28r56gnO6HxqzDJWR8IH3cuEbGCnhOIA1vvYT5eL2ex3tjTkfVfNR6anS03Mr53uo9EShiOOR815YOIoRXoQkeBcLMUcIRwkv4QrwLSIliDUUVHqqi_X5GWIMR9dXRm53CvFPxv8sdVr9GwAA__9Arn_Y) on a 500-acre Greene County wildfire Thursday. Flames [crossed into Hawkins County's Beech Creek community](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkbGupDAMRb8mdB4lIQRSUGxD97bdEpnEMNFmEhQ8w_L3K94vvNI6tqVz75-v-Qtjinn7jS8amdc503kkYqY677XsVPli_Odxf-dAdavlncOspbagFGg1o-f4odlgE8ZFK4fGNzSq3nW6c21rm-cY7GqGFckrdFL31nXKtW4wi257QiubON4PldJKKTl03eM-DUje635ozTIIIylELvXBT2LKmY6DaE1X-VB9-PJq0vhk3g_R_hJ6Eno6z_NxLvEbCj1h5egTCT3dfkJPqXhM915MYY31JlYC-kpwj7C8a455g0xYwWOmC3wl-gsJM8FWiTKBL-_MF3QSfMmMMVMQeuoU2FW1nQwBMNgVTPAEziw9YBsGDHjH4Zo6hv2MKcXD9sLI7YUxfbvwD4v4jPp_AAAA___vxJ1d) Thursday afternoon, and Baileyton Elementary closed for the day. ## Lawsuit Targets Airport Fuel Spills
The Flint Riverkeeper [sued the city of Atlanta](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0MFunDAQBuCnMTevsGHNcuCQtkFt1WyVNmpyQ4MZYNRZQPYs1r59tW3fIKc5jPTr__7Xp-4JiGmZznDBRqaxWzBFRhEMHVDY1iAMKV5JZIbld5xop6WzuXXaGG1NB15ox66EbGiKfEBTnjJsTFUf7bEuyyqbGzzVY--G2rrK1K53YPvjyY8uL6rBOQcZNfdAY6wxxuSlOxTG-qIfe--hr4fTUZU5DiRrOMiME65hIhj5tu4YDn69ZNzMIltUxYOyrbJtSumQYi_7_atse0cp2_Lqge_3n0h7BrpEXea5Hq_IOm7EHDUIwyKg__u1zAFBcNEj0yI60I5BJxAMOl63jW_Ktt9-fvrsXh6eq6-Prz8-nr-8PRe_3j58P788KttmoRm2RMwUXaXKfLoA8d_i8s7N98b-CQAA___tDpib) in federal court this week, alleging Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport has logged more than 400 fuel spills since July 2021. [At least nine](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL_GZEZ0Y2AIHFxCNpdeiBrbQOs8gEwP1v79itX8wSaVlPRUr_49xydx5G35S69gZZnHLeQzBpGQRuJ07Eki5fPNIitt_8-FL95GrLDVABphJCd8hdFQ4W1d-QDmUQQLXd9g0xvTFatt5n5qccK6642rut47ap0HjzDX1DVtwfYGAiAAQGXasgZ09TRPztHU-0ejTBU8y55KWcMS9rQwzfFrv0Iq3f4qol1FjlPVfxQOCoecc5mTz3epcLjpCgeAOzqFw0dJzxyD17QQb6dokkibkP546xuv53eI-thjfAvvm058hXQqHIpk_ZE5Rj7bTplqeRHHnzHyyx8vi98BAAD__1tCiQs) reached the Flint or its tributaries, the suit claims. The river flows beneath the airport's runways and supplies drinking water to about 400,000 Georgians. A jet fuel spill that began Jan. 30 sent about 28,000 gallons of fuel into the river and prompted a do-not-consume advisory in Griffin. The suit also cites sewage leaks and [elevated "forever chemical" levels](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkDGunTAQRVdjOj9hAw8oXKSh-2lTosEew-QbG9kDKLuPiN4O0s5cHZ17f33NX0CB4voTdjS8-jniXQIyY56B8pEyB7jLScwbxO-y0kVx1rV-S6WkVjNYpgvnFipnmtqhaocKjerHTndj2_bVZiwMQ4dO-8b6rh-hW3qn6kXX0MEwLO-KzANUSiulVN2-X43Stln8Yi0soxs60dboiFN-8YYrprwS-PAnXZhfNu1VMBvzUUTzQ-hJ6Om-75ddytPl-Qs9AQeIDEJPz1HoCeNFOcUdI0OQa07nUWQ5UX6S8oHLDTIXTxic_A32u6RY5JFCOJlSlMnLj0yRPlBkmenCLPRUZeOOm0Kg8u5FW687UPinyv-58mX03wAAAP__C8aXsQ) downstream. A city spokesperson said it would be inappropriate to comment on pending litigation. Flint Riverkeeper, represented by the Southern Environmental Law Center, says advocates spent more than a decade trying to work with the city.
## ATL Braces for Thanksgiving Rush
Hartsfield-Jackson [expects more than 4 million passengers](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkE-PlTAURz9N2fWFlvIoiy6IkRh1SDRxZp4bcimX0lj-pL2CfnuDceF-1r_k5Jzfy1P_BD741XWwoCE39SueKSARxh583LdIAc700xPNsP5Izh9-7WUu71wILkUPlvyBvYJsNEU-olA6QyOqupRlrVSVzUZXVY2QT0Vha6snrctK6nLS1agBQMvMmwsohBRCiFzdb4WQthimwVoY6lGXTOU4etrijWZ0uEXnYQq_twPjzW5LFsxMtCdWNEy2TLbned7ONNBxrUy2VxSTbdgsBCZboAArAf8XyPHXjpYSV3zxIfht5TukhKvDmPh_3Y5ThAMvxPvm68v37vX-3DXvXpvuw-fu0-P547fHl8sgi2bczwuV7hVTuVvAh7-i9MaPDyP_BAAA___WJJNt) during a Thanksgiving travel period that runs through Dec. 1, up 5% from last year. Airport officials projected yesterday as the busiest day, with [more than 364,000 passengers](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkDGv2yAUhX8N3hxxMSFhYOji7XXtaGG4xrePmAhuTd-_r5Kp-9uOdKRP53y_PpYPT5mO9NM_0HHalgN7y8iMdfFUn6Vy9r39IebdH58t0UnHoqQyI8CoYPGB6cRF-yG6SUYEfR_Qwc1e1dVqfRt2Z6WZ9C0aewUJxuLmbZSTlmG1qzfmPpB7AQEUAIDU5jKBCtO6rSH41cb7VWiJkbjUC--YsNREfstf5cR6CeUxZLczP5uYfgg1CzX33i-dS3iVQs0vulAzwDsLNe--ctsIcxx_-_DZyjHi3ycGbuNKKWHj8b-7aQy19NjGrVL0X0LNQ3Xx2SlnauYmtEwPT_m9hL8p8XTqXwAAAP__IZSHZQ). Sunday, Nov. 29, is expected to be another peak. Officials recommend arriving [21⁄2 hours before domestic flights](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1uhTAMBeCngS0ImwCXIUMXttu1IzKJgajhR4kLt29f0al7d8vnfOfjOTzJB7_N77SykXkaNr5SYBGOA_l47FECXenLiyy0fabZn34bsMRGASiEgaz4kwdNuTNV6Rj0I2cDbVdj3Wnd5otpJiRnsSu5phaB63asm5EcO9u0QFPuzf0QAAEASt0UFaCtxmm0lsbOPepMl-y87LGQhWfe4-xpCt_7ybGw-5oHs4gcKaveMuwz7K_rKqb9VZME2oTumwz7m5ZhTxIUvw62ktS6R1a3TOlV_RHOSiKdHDgmdXfLo3HH5UPwqWkzXc4r-fAbLf9c7TT4EwAA___Im4Sy) and three hours before international flights, and they warn of congestion on airport roads and curbsides. **Good Morning!** On this day in 1934, 17-year-old Ella Fitzgerald, a Newport News native, [_won the amateur night contest_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGO6yAQgOHT2F0sMwFsFxSvSZfXbmlN8GCPhCGCWaLcfrUr7Qm2__UV_8d9vSNHTvt_PMlJC2uiV40kQmX1OVUqDYVz2gsmqe_8KYfHFUawF6UuoFb0wo1Wjf3mAmrCpSenpsWAWYw1_eGmqwZ8oB3NOJtlVLPXNngfYEYg2GzP7ttTCpRSCjQMesKAdpqVsRQexnd6pI0ll0EOalx2TowhvnOjMvh89tEdIs_aXf91cOvg9tscXCWX95DL3sEt5Ubng0pf3PZ8cYxc7dTpcT-R448jf1zQHHwFAAD__wlNcoA) at Harlem's Apollo Theater. ## Virginia Awards Record $18.3M for Conservation
Virginia awarded a [record $18.3 million](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAMhp8GNhD2kQSGDF3YrmtHZHIGIoXklKRB9_YVVSt172b9n2x9_j_u852ss357p4N1Luvs-UyOc-Y4m-ATx0LZBr9F8jm9wmfeDc3YoWwAGoSZTLaF557qh16pZxpr1qBGgWIUUtS75rFTY7-YzixGkhykRFKDVAMpEHRTtdXXPQAEAMAe217RSlINICSvizBV3_HD5hDbvHOxcbPe0upeoXBsTThqp_ecn6m6vVU4VTid59luF_Uhtr8LV1LhdD0YQzh-xiayY0qcKpwujSsOhY-F41_k6eAGAMfxJhr27Z4PV0f9eJ7WOZukqvpuO8i6b5_8zyqLxq8AAAD__8KaiiA) to 23 conservation projects that will protect 8,091 acres, including farms, forests, battlefields, parks, and tribal lands. The grants include a [310-acre addition](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLtu6zAQBb-G6iSYaz6sgsVt1Pm2KYU1tZQY0KRBbSjo74MECJA-_cEZzLzd5zvGFPP6H5_kuIU507EnYqY6-5J3qg05lrxWzLyf5YM3jzNcwPRS9iBn9BwbzQq7xQVUhGNHTtpRgx610d3mUFuNdiS9gDJoUNINH0GG6808tNe-i-7rT0qQUkpQMCiLAY29SW0oPLQX6kJL5FIH3qjFusYcMaSzNKqDL88uuY35tYvrPwGTgOk4jmHxdfjZDmtpAqaEeel_WwmYWvKhf9XyTp77FHfuwwm2q255HTGluBsr1GV9YkzfKP5jpebgMwAA___1Hn9a) that will expand Shenandoah River State Park by nearly 20%, plus new local parks and additions to the natural-area preserve system. Separate awards will help the Monacan Indian Nation and Rappahannock Tribe expand protected lands, while a [$250,000 grant](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAQgOGnwVsiOAOOB4Yu3tK1o3XBh30SsSO4EuXtq3ToC3T_9Q3_13W-Imfe10-8U5CW5p2eNZMIlTkee6XSUPjY14K71NfxLVvEGTT4kzEnMDNG4UazxW4JCS3h2FEww-jAjc67bgtD1HiJBH0incDexpvulxG0T70fLzh0HN6eMWCMMWDhbAdM6IeLcZ7SzUVlNS0sRznLRo3Lyjtjyq-jUTnH497lsIk8quo_FEwKpr-mED0K1fquFEy9tu4ECqauhOXx5Jy5-kFZvd6R8y8l_7zQAvwEAAD__966cdc) will conserve Pipsico, a youth outdoor education center in Surry County.
## Ronald McDonald House Tops RVA 25
Ronald McDonald House Charities of Richmond [topped the inaugural](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkDGO3DAMRU9jdxpYXNkeFyrSuNu0KQ2OTFkEZGkgcTXYnD7wBDlBulc88n_8X5_bJ3LkdPzEk6w0vyV61UgiVDaXU6XSUDino2CS-p2_JDjcYIBJaa1Ab-iEG20G-916NIRLT1bPywjjMk5jH-wwLx4nvwOiu0_3ZcEFho-HMQRugMX3bK9_WoPWWoOBm5nR4zTf9TiRf4yuMwPtLLncJFDjcnBi9PE7Nyo3l88-2iDyrN3Hjw7WDtbCLpw57Q_-XSlVuqQO1iumg1XrN19eThh3dbr9L4T8VUn9u1aSn1VJIOW5VFHUqKjSUMGoUk7Pkj2LilxFvViC0mDUUfJLQgdrX-z-fHGMXKe5M8NxIsd3WfnPnZuFPwEAAP__xlOUcA) RVA 25 nonprofit list after averaging 124% annual revenue growth from 2023 through 2025. The charity attributed much of the growth to its $40 million capital campaign for a new Jackson Ward facility. It has raised $22 million toward its goal. RMHC Richmond [provides free lodging](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOrCAUxvGnwW6M51xQKShuYzfbbmmOgEqCMMEjk3n7zfoKW33dL_n-38_5SSGGtH3R4Q3XdU7-fUbP7Mtsczp9qcQhp61Q4vOTL94tzdhh_wB4IMxkOVQ_S2qcWUl60o03MGiFSqteNbtZ1eAsLNpZuTg56tFqa2F0fYcjaAdNML8eAAIAoMRWDrRSP4yger8uygrZeRc4l5Z3X0PZQgq0xk-uvrQ2H000O_PrFP_-C5wETiUniu6w7t49X_ePNpdN4ERLvvhxnQKnphj3eocYw9kPQnbbQSHeIv8xRjX4EwAA___pVXYp), meals, and support for families with hospitalized children. The new facility will eventually offer more than 60 rooms, with its first phase targeted to open by late 2028.
## Grant Expands Career Paths for Youth
The Boys & Girls Clubs of Central Virginia will receive a [$100,000 Bank of America grant](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOnDAQhJ8GOiN2zzZHQZGG7k-bEi32-rDis5HZH3JvH91JeYJ0U4xm5ptfX8sXxRTz4yc9eZIzLJmvI7EI18WVfHA9SWLJj0pZjlf5ls3Rgj1aBaAQFnIST140tX4KpJnGlicYRoNmNNa02wS91feAxvfWjf5G2nqgG6OFgb0zaxundx4AAgCgxk4PFMgOdzCWw2pco3v2UUrtZOMz1kfMkUJ6lZNr58qzTdMmsh_N7UeDc4PzdV2dWw8Y3zRvR4PzWzY4Q9__Vh8axX92yv5QjipzVWXfS5XvHCXyoUKpynGWSkn9q1Qf_gZnqhJd4mUNpFdnUVnje6WDM4qCW5XjO9K46vE-YLfJM7V18vsVU4qHHRrdP54U02e6_Ofr54R_AwAA__97rplu) to expand workforce-development programs helping young people prepare for careers and adulthood. The club's [Life and Workforce Readiness initiative](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOhCAQgOGnwU4jLKAWFNfY7bVXmhFHnATF4Cwb3_6y9wpX_8lX_D_P6QkU6QjfsKPjsk4Hvq-IzJgnn44LcwGmdIQMB193evHmYVKtsrWUtZITeKaCk4ZqcStohKFCJ7vBKDMYa6rNzeqxelyM1UtrBrSoe-tx9rbrO2kefUXu40mppJRSadXoDlawXS-NxXU2XugWF-KUG96wUA50EKzxTgVz49NeRbcxn5d4fAk1CjXOwcfX7As0KQehxjOnkGG_hBp1fWZKmfiu04t92rGGjPBJVXbL-aYY6bKd0G3YgeKfz_9cU5z6DQAA__8UcnqV) serves 830 young people with financial education, resume and interview preparation, career exploration, internships, college visits, and mentorships. The grant will provide $50,000 annually for two years, while the Neighborhood Builders award also includes leadership training and access to a national nonprofit network.
| Flying together with our sponsor [](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkMGOnDAMQL8GbjMamyTAgUOl1dy21x4jTzBgCRKUGFbz9xXbqj_Qq9-Tbb1fn_6TZJU4_6SNBz0nH_mrrKzK2YcUC-eTVFKcM0Ut73ToEsjjA90N4IbgKaic7A3V4zCRYeprHqDtLdreOlsvwxh6Z_iFDPia2I29IUOIzvYw4st0tQzXPgAEAECDd9PSRK7twDqeXjZU5sGjaMp3XfiUPEsUmtZ3OjnfQ9rqdVhU91I1Pyp8VviUeHLR-5yZY0jTxBzStlN8X_alNM9DN1_SkQNXzQdvJGuF7hpuPMqxVc3HTjLedsoaOZdF9r880LaTzPHb-Aehe9z61vo_UY4oSt520JiuQWj7Og_j_iXrKsW1lXnM18Hv1_U_q58D_g4AAP__A2eZWg) **The Company Warming up Wall Street** Coffee's the best way to start the morning. ## Trump Announces Pete Rose Pardon
President Donald Trump announced that he [posthumously pardoned Pete Rose](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2unTAQBOCngc7I3sNv4SIN3UmbEhl7ASvGa9nLQXn7iHsf4dYjzWi-P-_lbXzwcf9tTtRMx7ZEvEtAZsxLQsZMBZPJjiI6Pkz8W3b_WUBCL5QSoJaUqSS0vKja6RZfaptq1GqYOuimYezrQ6vBGuiHFR2OclilfZnVjsOkTC9HkF3t9VOoFCilVA99I1uzQdtaZ7dWdm6tWonOM-WGD6TD0xb-0QdzY-msgz6YU6levyqYK5jv-25um-gJK5hLosylgpnzdSZhYqQrWiwiUeHjOukq4vuh2CiL1RRcTQhiz2hYPAbiQaizdun2IfjSD1Ur99P48LXPP4b7aPgfAAD__4dNh3I), the Cincinnati Reds star whose 4,256 hits remain Major League Baseball’s career record. Rose pleaded guilty to two counts of [filing false tax returns](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAYBOCnwRsW_MF2PDB0YUvXjhYxPzEqBgR_YuXtK1fqE3Q-6XTffd2Wmw0xpMen3VFT3vyS8GgRibAuBQlrblhsdTmho82m7_YIrwUEjFxKDnIpNbeCKy2yc1rhRfq5Qy2neYBhnq5jt2npPQxutiuO84pK2RWmUQgUYMUA3nVBn4VSgpRSjjD2QlkPSq1u9UoM7s6UQBco1542zFvIPr7zC2u_5r2LeiMqjV0-GBgG5jiOHltJZ8jA7PHOwDTK9c3ALAxMcAzMIIaLkteJgTmd_ITykhttzz0_W3zzPzYvFVtwmIi7nGx0nOpzL13VrhwhxtDGiSnx2G2Iv4Po30--NPwEAAD__yCfixk) in 1990 and spent five months in federal prison. A year earlier, Rose had agreed to a [lifetime ban from baseball](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHO4yAQBOCnsTssFmOwC4pr3OXaKy3iXQd02CDYS5S3P-X_H-HvRzP65s9tu_mY4vX47U9ynMOxXfRqiZipboWYam5UfMV8EXLw19_2iM9NSWUEgFCwlZpboZ036NFpGuFYenJgl0lNi51NH5zBcZZkAcx9HtFYWABmO-E4WsAFZR_dpxBAAQAYZQap_aG03nE_tJzw3mlJGDnXgQPlEPOR3vlJddjz2ScXmEvrxl-dWju1tpIrt-HtQ86fQKdWXznuiVqn1lKpRaSLBebLJxRc_51FfBub-JgFTFKB1RaGwGfqq8PyiinFZmyn5eP0MX0t848vezr1PwAA__-RyYJP) after investigators found he bet on games while managing the Reds. MLB removed Rose from its permanently ineligible list in May 2025, about eight months after he died at 83. He could enter the National Baseball Hall of Fame as early as 2028.

On trade, he said a [deal with Mexico](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFutDAQhJ_GdEbeBcxRuPgbuvvblMjg9Z0jg5G9B8rbR1yRPEDK1Y5m5puP-3S3IYbt8d-uZNinaaOzRGKmPHF-rft1L2nzlGlbiLMNW55QoZYAEmGyC4eDJqic8URITUUG-qFDrYabrp4GafFtQx5ufX9D3brZKtc5apz2s8e5CuayA0AAaDR2dYcDts46T-B6GpRoFbnAKdefKWz8JB-_0kG5XtJaRfNk3oto_gkcBY7nedbLXK7a11_gGMNB8rU7y1QEjm8quWcqRf6CybeqcCa7yh88JXCssnH7GWIMRfeiVY_VhviO5r8Ndhj8DgAA__9mVIEt) is close after meeting President Claudia Sheinbaum. He also accused Iran of [refusing a real deal](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGuozAQheGnMV2QPRiDCxfb0GXbLZGXGScTGRuZ2aB9-6vcV7jl0ZG-4v9zX--RM5fH77hTkFTXQteZSYTaKu3ffnz2VkuiRmUjaZFLW0GDuxlzA7PGTfhNq-kwJCKgoaNgJj-C03523TOMMM92npPGtBk72jR5_Os8DIigEbHj8OGMAWPM4GDsR_BgMWIigxN5rawmZKmtf1Uu8qSU_9c3tX6re5fDU-Q41fBLwaJgua6rfx31lM-rYOEi1EoUriVmBUtswlummzej07ZrAY-Lc-bTTcrqxx45f7vysxrvAF8BAAD___A9dIU) to end the war and said he and Xi agreed to joint guardrails on AI. ## Feds Bust Major Train Robbery Ring
Federal prosecutors on Thursday charged 14 men in a Southern California [freight train theft ring](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFy7CAMRb8Gd3hANuxzQfEad5s2pYcYYZPF4AHtevL3GfYXUupqdOboft6Xuw0xpO3DHmjI5yXhVSMSYVmoPI-zzWtOHgumFanYkMoCAjSXkoNc7ErhhYvsnPGIgEOHRt4mBVpM_3S3GyG0AHR-nBx6BD0o4ZUatVBoQamhC6bhpAQp5aBB9QomGJ11HqW74STYKNAFyqX_ziHRjj7-5BeWfs1HF81OdFY2_GcwM5iv6-rXr9q0257BHHO1acOIlcHccgZzzU_asSS-2hh8LilY_v6N7xgq8RLSxo8QY8ip8ko5YuIpPLC29LLPByI_84WFU86xIbti3Hm1k6pvbBTbYUN8K9Lfin0Z-A0AAP__DmGRqw) accused of stealing more than $22.5 million in Nike sneakers, Milwaukee tools, and electronics from at least 36 trains. The crew cut air hoses to force the trains into emergency stops, then sawed into cargo containers while lookouts watched the tracks, prosecutors said. [See the video](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGu3CAYhE-DO1bwY7NL4SJS5O6lTWmxMNgkGFaYZyc5feS9witHI42--X5-zB82ppiXH3bD2EKZM849oTXUudXP7XVlV3JARXZo1cZcZxKkuZSc5Gxdiwdm2fkxAATVYZR3M5AW5qG7dVTDw_XCSwjSfRjs0D-8N94FBRnI6S6O15yUJKVUmobbQIZ6b32A9HcYwXoBH1upt18l5rYipL_lQL25snVpXFt77Ux9YzQxms7zvIXy58K-ekbT585oCvA7r0iwO_iz2n_IfEXcGz-iR-FutXUBlz23KWGB50R82LizKYZSc7Q8VMRlbfztgF8YjdeYF6ambS_ud_RMfRdPofRDKxPIaIIVMPL-1MEgCK1M39XRv86YUtz1nfVi2WxM7yPta_qPkf4HAAD__2wrmkc) released by investigators. The operation was run by 21-year-old Nathan Angel from East Los Angeles alongside his father and two uncles, and the goods went to stash houses, according to the indictment. Agents [raided an apartment](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGOgzAQRU9jOkfMACYuXGxDl223RAaPg1fGRvYkUW6_IlfYZqTRl57--z-3-WZDDOn-bXcy7POc6FUjMVOZuTz24_zXnDwVSitxsSGVGVtUEkAizHbl8KQZGmc8EVLXkIFRD6hafVXNZhavV9UTgl96p0ZvuwEWZcdBw9VpoCaYEweAANApHC4DauyddZ7AjaRb0bfkAudy-c0h8UY-vvOTymXNexPNxnxU0X0JnARO6X3kymckcDrBAieA82iB06PKU0jg5MlVWWxwsubVRrnlnaRluVJiKjJ7ibjLj68seVmovGUJ6S5waopxxyvEGKoaRd_edxvipwz_b8Knwb8AAAD__5ZRhTI) at the center of the case Thursday morning. All 14 face conspiracy charges, and two are also charged with violence against railroad carriers. Thirteen of them were arrested Thursday and arraigned in federal court in Los Angeles.

## Dallas ISD Joins Wave of School Closures
Dallas ISD trustees [voted Thursday](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2upSAUBeCnwY4T2HL9KSimsbvTTmk2sFGSrRhh9Jy3nzivcOsvWVlr_fmevzFx2pffuJGt75jnne7CVCudc0R-bMFynMlTWT8HnSXvaQYFndRagp7R13TRrJtgnQqjbsjqfvyCDow2zWpRoR4dtH3AdvBu9DT6SIPDEGPvY9sk-6RpDVqDUtq8CMCZL6_jEJ1R0AmjKKSaz1ddqdIbS-RPvuh8-bw1bNdajyLaXwImAdN936_d-RDvhwVMzyABE2ePLGAKyIxFphIkHseZLyryYNxlzdJzLiRLesvi15y5SNxSkO5vWKjKQDH5VAVMRquhh0HA1Jw2HHdiTqXrhVHLhon_96o_vPOy8C8AAP__1D-MWg) to close six campuses starting in the 2027-28 school year as the district faces a projected $128 million shortfall. Leaders blamed inflation, reduced state funding, and enrollment more than 3,000 students below projections. The [6-3 vote](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOozAQhJ8GOiPvxkAoXFxDl2uvRMZegyWDkdeB5O1P_K_wdyPNaEbz_XtNLxNi2Je_ZiNdPj5NO10cqRTKkzfx9hbDRw6WeP0elDntYUKJnQAQCJOxJZw0Qe30LN0ANWnohxY7VKDqVbePp3GW2oEeyvmh7U3fw0CzbJUHhV0d9N0GgAAoJaiGEGfVWvBPPyuJXaUkuVBSbspKhT6Gffymk3Jj01ZHvZZycPX4U-FY4XhdV-PTR90_7kCF4y0rHJ2J0bAI7MSZCrGwMTGJTlizHW8mFmYLTsxvt1ARNu2W8s511u64QoyBu75SctlMiD_L5ZfATo3_AwAA__8aEYIF) came after three trustees, including Byron Sanders, failed to spare J.J. Rhoads, a South Dallas pre-K the district chose to reopen in 2019. Also closing is Harrell Budd Elementary, which has received two failing state ratings in three years. Dallas isn't alone. Texas public schools lost about 75,000 students last school year, [state education officials reported](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOozAQhJ_GdEb2xjGhcHENXa69Epn1EiwtGNlOSN7-RKT_Cf5y99OMZubffbz7yHF7_PUrufqe07jRUZhqpTzOnk_28GXPEaksn51ySVscQYGVWkvQo8caXzTqJrhJhV435HTXX8GC0aZZnDV27ju63EzA3oJXtsO-V1ej0ILB0ER3umkNWoNS2rQEMJkr6vk2T0aBFUZRiDXlti5U6e3LzJ_0otxiWht2S617EZc_AgYBw3EcLU7lrHFyAcNXImA4Xz-n3J8TR5QFl5S4yEDIcSNJW07MK21VIqfyzCQreQFDk13Yj8gci-2EUY_VR_4GqL_c7eXgfwAAAP__ZACETQ), and a demographer warned lawmakers that this year's drop could top 120,000. Fort Worth ISD alone plans to close 19 campuses.
## Darlie Routier Cites New DNA Evidence
Attorneys for Darlie Routier, on death row for the 1996 fatal stabbing of her 5-year-old son, [filed a new appeal](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2upSAUhZ8GOwx7H_wrKKaxu9NOaRA2RxIEA1w9vv3EmUe45cqXrKz1_flavrQPPr5_651U_bi0RLpKoFopL06Hh711ObI3VLb7oFxS9AsK7DkAR1i0qf6kBRqrVmEnaEjBMHXYowTZbEqIzoyjcL2ZxMtYGsDI1zp0k-5W69ax8eppA0AAFAJkS4ir7Ay40a1SYM-kIOtrym3dqNJHFxfudFJuTdqboLZaj8JevxjODOfrutq4GuuuBzOcn0MM55CMDv8jt1FzOr2laIhnCqQLWe4jtzoHTzyn7-opFw7T1PP9O1vK3OhCXNeacqS78KJvhrMEMfadZDg3Wdnj8iH40g9Miveuffi3sP5Q7KnwbwAAAP__0juOZg) Thursday citing DNA and fingerprint evidence they say supports her claim that an intruder killed him and his 6-year-old brother. The filing says [advanced DNA testing](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGutCAQhZ8GOwyM6GpB8Td2-7e3NAijToJggNXdt79xX-GWM1_OyTnn5zk9DXkK63-zoy7vJU4Br-yxFEzTYvzNVpOPRBbz9jkw5RhoAgEdl5KDnIwtdOIkK6dn4QZZoZaPoYUOlFTVpru2aZ0bGhCt7YWCHlpomqHv5dAgtKYifbtJCVKCEFLVCDCr1sqlX2YloGNKoKMSU102LPg2efGfeGKqbdwrr7dSjsyafwxGBuN1XbWd813j5gzGr4TBeL_uc0uI3KE1DjP3pmDiAS_uguF4ksNgkSf0aDI67kzyhDzFVyFM3G7kHd9fyWHiFE7MhVZTKAYGY5W0Oy7ynnL3YEqsuyH_DVn-uO2p4TcAAP__IuyRCQ) found an unidentified man's genetic material on a bloody sock in an alley behind her Rowlett home. New fingerprint exams excluded Routier and her then-husband as the source of prints on a door and a knife, though the source remains unknown. Her lawyers want the Court of Criminal Appeals to return the case to a trial court. [Two earlier appeals](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uqzAMx58GtqDYDdAOGe7C1rveEZnElEghoMSF9u2vOK9wNks_6__17zk-KcSQXn9pZSufeRsTnyWyCOdxpnixF5U9B8dl-e6cy5bCiBo7BaAQRnISDh6h9nbS_gE1W-gfLXZowNSL9a2mjqd-ZofcE0zdnVrXw-3uvUbAOthLDQABUGswDSNOpnUw3-fJaOwqo9kH2XIjCwt_qMzxux2cG7etdbSLyF6q258KhwqH8zybefuYq8f1UOFwnRUOnnIMrPL2lsBZ0b4zReWCcFGJT-UTKT6C5-RYkQivu6jLR945Kc8kiyqc5OJ1tn4_Q4yhdH1l9GulEH_yyC9nPCz-DwAA__-oXot3) failed, but neither involved new DNA. Let’s be abundantly clear:
**Black women are the backbone of the Democratic Party.**
On Election Day, 93% of Black women voted for Democrats. They knocked the doors. They organized their churches, their families, and their neighborhoods. They turned out across the Deep South in numbers that stunned the experts, and they delivered the blue wave that just won us the House and the Senate.
Every time our backs were against the wall, Black women showed up.
And far too often, the party thanked them with a speech and then moved on.
Not this time.
On December 12, we have a chance to do more than say thank you. We have a chance to make history:

clean_body: Black women are the backbone of the Democratic Party. | | | == Let’s be abundantly clear: Black women are the backbone of the Democratic Party. On Election Day, 93% of Black women voted for Democrats. They knocked the doors. They organized their churches, their families, and their neighborhoods. They turned out across the Deep South in numbers that stunned the experts, and they delivered the blue wave that just won us the House and the Senate. Every time our backs were against the wall, Black women showed up. And far too often, the party thanked them with a speech and then moved on. Not this time. On December 12, we have a chance to do more than say thank you. We have a chance to make history: == Rep. Patricia “Pat” Moore (D) is headed to a runoff. If she wins, she’ll be the first Black woman Louisiana has EVER sent to Congress. Pat has spent 19 years serving her community in Monroe, first on the Ouachita Parish Police Jury and now in the state House. She’s exactly the kind of leader Black women have built this party around for generations, and exactly the kind of leader they deserve to see in Washington. But MAGA won’t hand this seat over. Republicans have held it since 2004, and they’ll fight with everything they have to keep it. Black women have shown up for Democrats every single time. Washington's two parties disagree on almost everything, but this week they achieved rare consensus on one thing: the enemy within. On one side of the Capitol, a former president's memoir is settling two-year-old scores with the speaker, the Senate leader, and one very famous former president who eased him off his own ticket. On the other, two of the administration's most senior Cabinet officers are conducting a blame exchange over Chinese microchips, with a business-news network serving as neutral ground. Two civil wars, one capital. Both sides should take a long look at what this infighting is doing to them -- because the damage compounds, and it compounds in exactly the ways that make unity going forward harder, not easier.
**An Italian lunch, a funeral truce, and a grudge in hardcover**
Joe Biden's new book, 'Promise Me, America', arrives next week, and his office has spent the past week drip-releasing its angriest passages like a hostage negotiation. The centerpiece is his mended friendship with Nancy Pelosi: an Italian lunch, decades of shared history, warm words about falling "into the old rhythms of friendship." It reads like reconciliation until you keep reading -- because Biden cannot help re-fighting the war.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1a85fcde-753a-4904-9dad-beb8b729df51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
He writes that Pelosi was "working furiously behind the scenes to get elected officials and Biden delegates to defect." He recalls Chuck Schumer driving to his Delaware home on July 13, 2024, to inform him that his support in the party had collapsed, and allows that he "told Schumer he had a lot of gumption (I may have said it differently at the time), coming to my home and telling me to get out of the race." Barack Obama, who worked his own behind-the-scenes levers, received no phone call on the way out -- an omission made more pointed by the report that Biden was "furious" with Obama for working against him. Kamala Harris, he writes, "asked me several times if I was sure I wanted to do this" -- her caution preserved to the minute. Bill Clinton got his call at 3:14 p.m., timestamped for posterity, because that is what this book is: a diary with a publicist.
The through-line is loyalty. "Loyalty matters to me," Biden writes. "If I give you my word, I stick with you. If I say I'm with you, I'm with you to the end." A moving sentiment -- about other people's loyalty. About his own, the less said the better; the book calls the Atlanta debate "a terrible night" and then offers no ground on any of the fallout, striking the defensive tone that defined the final two years.
Jill Biden, out on her own book tour, told MS NOW's "Morning Joe" that the peace was actually sealed at Tatiana Schlossberg's funeral: "He went back to see Nancy and I found out later ... they said 'Peace, let's be friends.'" A truce brokered at a funeral tells you exactly where this relationship had been. And Biden concedes that when the two finally sat down together, they didn't discuss the episode at all. That is not mending a fence. That is painting over it and scheduling the sequel.
From where this column sits, the Democratic wound was self-inflicted twice over. First, the party that campaigned on democracy as the central issue of our time resolved its own nomination question through lunch summits and delegate defections rather than ballots. Biden insists that "Party unity was weighing heavily on my mind. I believed the Democratic rank and file were still with me and would be with me all the way to November. But it was clear that major Democratic elected officials and leaders weren't." Maybe the rank and file were. They were never permitted to find out. And Biden lands on the sentence that doubles as this column's thesis: "I had arrived at exactly what I had most hoped to avoid: a divided party."
Going forward, the anger does not retire with the book tour. The party's three most senior living figures -- Pelosi, Schumer, Obama -- now stand accused in hardcover of betraying their own president. Everyone who wants to run in 2028 has now learned two things: the score-keeping is permanent, and every friendship comes with a memoir clause. A ceasefire with a publication date is not unity.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/30d8712e-3744-4240-a606-ff00f41c1c01?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**" Commerce has the pen"**
The Republican civil war is younger, and in one important respect more serious: it is actually about something. The stakes are Chinese microchips, not lunch reservations.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent went on CNBC Friday and, in the politest possible dialect, accused Howard Lutnick's Commerce Department of burying an interagency recommendation. Treasury, State, the Pentagon, and the U.S. Trade Representative all favored placing Megaspeed -- an Nvidia customer long suspected of circumventing U.S. law and funneling advanced chips into China -- on Commerce's entity list of national-security-risk companies. "Commerce ... has the pen," Bessent said. "You would have to ask them about their internal processes." He added that the president "made it very clear" that China should not receive Nvidia chips above a certain technological level, "and so any leakage is very frustrating because it hurts our great companies in the AI race, gives the Chinese an advantage."
The feud has a body count. It detonated days after the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who stepped down amid reports of an affair with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive suspected of having intelligence connections to Beijing. Senior Trump officials -- Lutnick included -- were briefed on that relationship months ago, and Commerce declined to blacklist Megaspeed anyway. Bessent confronted Lutnick in a tense Situation Room meeting last week; asked about it on Friday, he offered the quote of the week: "We don't repeat conversations in the Situation Room." Now some of the president's advisers are discussing whether Lutnick should be dismissed, outside advisers are calling the president to raise alarm bells, and the White House, for the moment, is standing by the man it calls "the most transformative Commerce Secretary in modern history."
On the merits, Bessent has the better of the argument. When four agencies concur and the president's own directive sits unexecuted, "internal processes" is not an answer; it is the accusation. But the merits are precisely what the spectacle is burying. A Cabinet-level knife fight conducted on business television, over China policy, is programming Beijing will study frame by frame. An administration built on loyalty is now running loyalty tribunals against itself, in public, while the question the fight is supposedly about -- who is letting chips leak to a strategic rival -- goes unanswered. Whatever Lutnick's fate, the airing itself is the self-inflicted wound.
**Why both wars matter going forward**
Strip away the settings -- an Italian restaurant, a Situation Room -- and the two stories are the same story. In each, a party's internal dispute has graduated from private counsel to public vendetta. In each, the combatants are aiming not at the opposition but at their own side's seniors, colleagues, and former friends. And in each, the weapon of choice is the same: the permanent record. The memoir, the televised accusation, the well-sourced leak -- instruments designed not to win the argument but to fix blame forever.
That instinct is understandable. It is also, going forward, poisonous -- for four reasons.
First, trust does not survive the ledger. Democratic voters learned that their party's leadership treated the fitness of its own elected standard-bearer as a management problem to be handled over one lunch. Republican voters are learning that their Cabinet secretaries will take a dispute to CNBC before they take one to the president. Each public war teaches partisans that their own side's institutions cannot be believed -- and cynical partisans make poor soldiers for anyone's coalition.
Second, governance becomes a by-product. Treasury is prosecuting an export-control dispute through morning television; the Democratic Party's most senior statesman is managing the seating chart of a two-year-old lunch. The AI race does not pause for the infighting. Neither does China, which continues to treat America's civil wars as free strategic intelligence.
Third, the next cycle inherits the enemies list. Biden's book is effectively a map of who owes what to whom, and every 2028 Democrat will read it the way a sailor reads weather. On the right, whoever lines up to defend or condemn Lutnick is enlisting in a conflict whose boundaries are not yet drawn. Ambition follows grievance, and grievance is now being stockpiled in both camps at industrial scale.
Fourth -- and this is the part both parties keep learning the hard way -- peace purchased with silence has an expiration date. The Democratic model was a funeral truce and an Italian lunch at which the actual subject was never discussed. It held, briefly and beautifully, right up until the manuscript deadline. The Republican model -- a public confidence statement and a public blame assignment in the same news cycle -- is not even pretending to reconcile.
Biden's line -- "If I say I'm with you, I'm with you to the end" -- is genuinely moving, and both parties spent this week proving its modern corollary: the end comes sooner than it used to, and when it arrives there is a book deal. If either party wants unity going forward, the first step is not an Italian lunch or a cable hit. It is having the argument inside the family, in the room, and then closing the door. Everything else -- the diary timestamps, the CNBC segues, the funeral handshakes -- is just the civil war, serialized.

clean_body: Both Parties Are at War With Themselves | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? Both Parties Are at War With Themselves | | | Nov 21 | | | | | | | | | | | | Washington's two parties disagree on almost everything, but this week they achieved rare consensus on one thing: the enemy within. On one side of the Capitol, a former president's memoir is settling two-year-old scores with the speaker, the Senate leader, and one very famous former president who eased him off his own ticket. On the other, two of the administration's most senior Cabinet officers are conducting a blame exchange over Chinese microchips, with a business-news network serving as neutral ground. Two civil wars, one capital. Both sides should take a long look at what this infighting is doing to them -- because the damage compounds, and it compounds in exactly the ways that make unity going forward harder, not easier. An Italian lunch, a funeral truce, and a grudge in hardcover Joe Biden's new book, 'Promise Me, America', arrives next week, and his office has spent the past week drip-releasing its angriest passages like a hostage negotiation. The centerpiece is his mended friendship with Nancy Pelosi: an Italian lunch, decades of shared history, warm words about falling "into the old rhythms of friendship." It reads like reconciliation until you keep reading -- because Biden cannot help re-fighting the war. | | ---|---|--- He writes that Pelosi was "working furiously behind the scenes to get elected officials and Biden delegates to defect." He recalls Chuck Schumer driving to his Delaware home on July 13, 2024, to inform him that his support in the party had collapsed, and allows that he "told Schumer he had a lot of gumption (I may have said it differently at the time), coming to my home and telling me to get out of the race." Barack Obama, who worked his own behind-the-scenes levers, received no phone call on the way out -- an omission made more pointed by the report that Biden was "furious" with Obama for working against him. Kamala Harris, he writes, "asked me several times if I was sure I wanted to do this" -- her caution preserved to the minute. Bill Clinton got his call at 3:14 p.m., timestamped for posterity, because that is what this book is: a diary with a publicist. The through-line is loyalty. "Loyalty matters to me," Biden writes. "If I give you my word, I stick with you. If I say I'm with you, I'm with you to the end." A moving sentiment -- about other people's loyalty. About his own, the less said the better; the book calls the Atlanta debate "a terrible night" and then offers no ground on any of the fallout, striking the defensive tone that defined the final two years. Jill Biden, out on her own book tour, told MS NOW's "Morning Joe" that the peace was actually sealed at Tatiana Schlossberg's funeral: "He went back to see Nancy and I found out later ... they said 'Peace, let's be friends.'" A truce brokered at a funeral tells you exactly where this relationship had been. And Biden concedes that when the two finally sat down together, they didn't discuss the episode at all. That is not mending a fence. That is painting over it and scheduling the sequel. From where this column sits, the Democratic wound was self-inflicted twice over. First, the party that campaigned on democracy as the central issue of our time resolved its own nomination question through lunch summits and delegate defections rather than ballots. Biden insists that "Party unity was weighing heavily on my mind. I believed the Democratic rank and file were still with me and would be with me all the way to November. But it was clear that major Democratic elected officials and leaders weren't." Maybe the rank and file were. They were never permitted to find out. And Biden lands on the sentence that doubles as this column's thesis: "I had arrived at exactly what I had most hoped to avoid: a divided party." Going forward, the anger does not retire with the book tour. The party's three most senior living figures -- Pelosi, Schumer, Obama -- now stand accused in hardcover of betraying their own president. Everyone who wants to run in 2028 has now learned two things: the score-keeping is permanent, and every friendship comes with a memoir clause. A ceasefire with a publication date is not unity. | | ---|---|--- " Commerce has the pen" The Republican civil war is younger, and in one important respect more serious: it is actually about something. The stakes are Chinese microchips, not lunch reservations. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent went on CNBC Friday and, in the politest possible dialect, accused Howard Lutnick's Commerce Department of burying an interagency recommendation. Treasury, State, the Pentagon, and the U.S. Trade Representative all favored placing Megaspeed -- an Nvidia customer long suspected of circumventing U.S. law and funneling advanced chips into China -- on Commerce's entity list of national-security-risk companies. "Commerce ... has the pen," Bessent said. "You would have to ask them about their internal processes." He added that the president "made it very clear" that China should not receive Nvidia chips above a certain technological level, "and so any leakage is very frustrating because it hurts our great companies in the AI race, gives the Chinese an advantage." The feud has a body count. It detonated days after the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who stepped down amid reports of an affair with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive suspected of having intelligence connections to Beijing. Senior Trump officials -- Lutnick included -- were briefed on that relationship months ago, and Commerce declined to blacklist Megaspeed anyway. Bessent confronted Lutnick in a tense Situation Room meeting last week; asked about it on Friday, he offered the quote of the week: "We don't repeat conversations in the Situation Room." Now some of the president's advisers are discussing whether Lutnick should be dismissed, outside advisers are calling the president to raise alarm bells, and the White House, for the moment, is standing by the man it calls "the most transformative Commerce Secretary in modern history." On the merits, Bessent has the better of the argument. When four agencies concur and the president's own directive sits unexecuted, "internal processes" is not an answer; it is the accusation. But the merits are precisely what the spectacle is burying. A Cabinet-level knife fight conducted on business television, over China policy, is programming Beijing will study frame by frame. An administration built on loyalty is now running loyalty tribunals against itself, in public, while the question the fight is supposedly about -- who is letting chips leak to a strategic rival -- goes unanswered. Whatever Lutnick's fate, the airing itself is the self-inflicted wound. Why both wars matter going forward Strip away the settings -- an Italian restaurant, a Situation Room -- and the two stories are the same story. In each, a party's internal dispute has graduated from private counsel to public vendetta. In each, the combatants are aiming not at the opposition but at their own side's seniors, colleagues, and former friends. And in each, the weapon of choice is the same: the permanent record. The memoir, the televised accusation, the well-sourced leak -- instruments designed not to win the argument but to fix blame forever. That instinct is understandable. It is also, going forward, poisonous -- for four reasons. First, trust does not survive the ledger. Democratic voters learned that their party's leadership treated the fitness of its own elected standard-bearer as a management problem to be handled over one lunch. Republican voters are learning that their Cabinet secretaries will take a dispute to CNBC before they take one to the president. Each public war teaches partisans that their own side's institutions cannot be believed -- and cynical partisans make poor soldiers for anyone's coalition. Second, governance becomes a by-product. Treasury is prosecuting an export-control dispute through morning television; the Democratic Party's most senior statesman is managing the seating chart of a two-year-old lunch. The AI race does not pause for the infighting. Neither does China, which continues to treat America's civil wars as free strategic intelligence. Third, the next cycle inherits the enemies list. Biden's book is effectively a map of who owes what to whom, and every 2028 Democrat will read it the way a sailor reads weather. On the right, whoever lines up to defend or condemn Lutnick is enlisting in a conflict whose boundaries are not yet drawn. Ambition follows grievance, and grievance is now being stockpiled in both camps at industrial scale. Fourth -- and this is the part both parties keep learning the hard way -- peace purchased with silence has an expiration date. The Democratic model was a funeral truce and an Italian lunch at which the actual subject was never discussed. It held, briefly and beautifully, right up until the manuscript deadline. The Republican model -- a public confidence statement and a public blame assignment in the same news cycle -- is not even pretending to reconcile. Biden's line -- "If I say I'm with you, I'm with you to the end" -- is genuinely moving, and both parties spent this week proving its modern corollary: the end comes sooner than it used to, and when it arrives there is a book deal. If either party wants unity going forward, the first step is not an Italian lunch or a cable hit. It is having the argument inside the family, in the room, and then closing the door. Everything else -- the diary timestamps, the CNBC segues, the funeral handshakes -- is just the civil war, serialized. You're currently a free subscriber to . ## Senators Sue over Amendment 87
Two Republican state senators [sued Thursday to stop Colorado from collecting](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLuunEAMhp8GulkxXi6bgiIN3UmbEhljWOvMjFczXkjePiJKnuCUln99_-Xnx_yBEiTtPzDyaLTNic8S2IzzjJHTGjnZYyhvsUX2rPQpXGZooHfeO_AzksnBc4v1Om4bEPY1j3741kHfe9_Vz7FrlraDlbau2zx0g28JHoD3pQfCpeFaxovnPXh_b3zX3mCA9QH0aBHbhfp71Ta8imm-2ZNJg2ZcdQu_9eB8I411GJ9mr1Ldv1cwVTCd53lbOR2ch-tfwXTVqmAKShjcvwNcMTR2hROa5uLKm52pW4LSp_vvUy65k0Qa2Rn-chRQoqTdHWqci9vVnCQkeueLJmnTHNFEU53H9XVKCFL6oWqbPaKEv4Hti1sfI_wJAAD__2L0l6Y) the higher income taxes voters approved under Amendment 87. Sens. Barbara Kirkmeyer and Byron Pelton argue the measure violated TABOR by [bundling a constitutional change with tax-rate increases](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkDtuwzAQRE8jdTTIFUXKBYs06pw2pbCmVhIRfgxxbcW3DxwguUDqGQzmvY_LdMEQQ17fMZFjv0yZjhqJmfYJE-U5UebB1nvga1j34j8D1QkkGKGUADWh5_CgSWM7u2UBj6Ylp-y5B2OU6tvNDdLCIq3F3s9yMANeZb8oYwBQd3TWbXCvPaVAqU6qXp_AwjyAHzSivnrTNVrSHLjsJ97Il1h2nMsSn-VB-8mX1Ea3Md9q0701MDYwcq2_tVfewJjpEBGPF4dAZko3roKLyPcYw_IUIfuSSDB-Cb9hXqmKkMWfATHYBsZ2d_PtCDGGamyj5ZowxJ8D_E93DwffAQAA__8r4YUI) in one ballot question. They also claim the Blue Book wrongly told [about 55,000 taxpayers](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAQhp8Gd1hmgsFXUFzjLtdeaY2HcYIOmwi4ePP2K1bKvsCWM6Nv9H__3-tyxRDDcfuDO7tK23LwWSLXynnBnQ-_81EnW_6HuoZbTvQvcFlgACOVkqAWpBqevGjsvNs2IDQdO2V_jWCMUmN3d9pvdoJtXO26jhOTMZa8tgyGCNQwdMG1f0qBUpdBjboHC34CmjSiXslchB7Yh5pyX-9MKaaMPm3xlZ6ce0p7F9291kcRl98CZgHzeZ49raW5tLuA-U0JmNtWwBzxbFby21JOVmYMhWXFDy7yjbTxgS_Ojeqy848zxBiKsUIPtx1D_MpQf1jf08FnAAAA__9E7YaS) earning $500,000 to $1 million they'd get a tax cut. Chris deGruy Kennedy of the Bell Policy Center, which helped pass the measure, called the suit "totally frivolous." He said the Colorado Supreme Court already settled the single-subject question. The amendment passed with 51.7% of the vote and takes effect Jan. 1. It replaces the flat 4.4% rate with brackets topping out at 8.4%.
## Kiros Votes against Jeffries
Denver Rep.-elect Melat Kiros was [one of 11 House Democrats](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkDGypCAURVeDGZY8EemAYBKznnRC6zU8WkYUCxip2f2v_lv4-a1b55w_z_WJIYbz_RsPMtX69aRWItVKecWDTnfQWfVc_oX6Cu-c7B6orDCA4kJwECvaGm5aJXbOeA8WVUdGzI8JlBJi6jZjtdTeWxqnQQvtB60IURN5ackqlF0wnz8hQIhxEJPsYQanwWqJKF9WjUwO5EJNua8b2RRTRpd8_J9uyr1NRxfNVutV2PiLwcJgaa31jUptKbvPgMHy8WKwODpvyoUfFLHyPeRUeLquVKjwDXeig_8l73OgwstFuFPmcngoKWfBYOmycVcLMYaiZiaH94EhfiPUH9a7DXwFAAD__yEdhdc) who voted against nominating Hakeem Jeffries for speaker in Wednesday's closed-door caucus vote. Jeffries won the nomination 251-11 and still faces a full House vote in January. Kiros and six other incoming members said in a joint statement that their priorities include Medicare for All, curbing ICE enforcement, getting money out of politics, and ending the war in Gaza. Kiros, a 29-year-old democratic socialist, [defeated longtime Rep. Diana DeGette](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkbGu3CAQRb_G7ljBmAVTuEjj7qVNaWEY26NgWMHsWvn7yJHyBa87mpHu1dH99bV8eUqU95_-xInDtmS8WkJmrIs_MccTM4-2vYlX2msJvwnbAhKMUEqAWnxg-uCifR-nbYPgTY-Tsu4Jxij17I9JonSriwMGb01AiaO0blBewqoRpetpuvOUAqUGqZ76ARbiCGHU3us1mKHTEiNxqQ8-MJRUqo9lS3_KB-sjlLNP08H8at3wo4O5g_m6roe7Te5vB7OvTCFhB_N97GB-lURM4UZMGJhKvvnAik1cR2mivnOmvIutVPG_sgnVWISS94qtUck-iUiNKwXuYLaDGLSRRhonMIAXGtAJb0ct4ioRYtTWoerrFF8XpUTN2E7L_fSU_mnwNxf4TPA3AAD__-3dmsg) in the June primary and [won the 1st Congressional District](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO2zAQRL-G6miIK4rSFSzSqLu0KYX1cmVvjhINcmMhfx84gL_g2hm8wcz8-lw_UbIct5-4c1Ta1oPPllmV64o7H2nnQ-ep_RG9yq0W-hJuK_QQrHMW3Iqk8uTVY5fitgFh6Di66WOEEJwbu3t03m8wDtwPFHAMIwN_zNs1TPPIQ0LXSXzlOQfODb0b_QUmSDPQ7BH9lcJgfM9JtNSL3plKLhVT2fLf8uR6obJ3Od5VH80MPwwsBpbzPC90ba8tL9_A8qYMLC_VwJJ4L1RRhWwrJJilqd05o9ovqaXZRy2_mZSTfcPWNbVUjlvl1qQcmG2SplVIDSxdjelxSs7SwmR8f9tR8v96-s1nnxH-BQAA__8tBJEY) with about 78% of the vote. She has said Democrats need to "change course."
## Rockies Trade for Two Starters
The Rockies [acquired right-handers Luis Castillo and Davis Martin](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkL2unDAQhZ8GukF4MD-3cJGG7qZNiQZ7WEYxeGPPQvL20UaR8gDpjnSko_N93z6XT5Io5-MrHezUb8vJd4msynmhg89w8KnTWF6iqzxy8t-Fy4ItDmAMoFnIq1y8WKqD2zb0NNTszPjR4zAY09e7-8AeDTF27YDtZEKwLfkex26dcN1GW4t77xmDxnSt6W2DI4YJ_WSJ7OqHrrItB9GUG93Zp5gyhbTFX-ni3Ph01NHtqs9SdV8qnCuc7_tuAp8X5_HdVziXZ8paKpz_IvxLQP7HSzKD7pkZVA4GihGKUob4kgKeikqMCQJdUuCgrHKCnKCZAsMtusO9izKU9LPOLjxviVHKMFa2fRwk8c9J_U-_l8PfAQAA___ZCZKk) from the White Sox on Thursday, sending away left-hander Sean Sullivan and 17-year-old catching prospect Douglas Veliz. Castillo, 33, is a three-time All-Star, but he went 4-11 with a 5.85 ERA in 2026 while splitting time between Seattle and Chicago. Martin, 29, had his best season, going 9-8 with a 3.95 ERA in 28 starts. By the time the polls closed on the West Coast last Tuesday, the shorthand was already circulating in the group chats and the green rooms: checkmate. Not check. Checkmate.
For two years we were told, endlessly and often by people who should have known better, that Donald Trump was playing four-dimensional chess. Every tariff was a feint. Every raid was a demonstration of leverage. Every norm shattered was a rook sacrificed for positional advantage we lesser minds simply could not see. The phrase became a reflex, a theological claim about a man who never loses because losing is for people who play in fewer dimensions.
Well. The chessboard has been set out now, all sixty-four squares of it, and the position speaks for itself. Democrats won roughly 254 House seats to the Republicans' 165, with more still trickling in from California. They took the Senate going away -- 54 seats called, with Alaska and Mississippi still leaning blue, a state Trump carried by thirteen points and a state he carried by twenty-six. Mary Peltola, a Democrat, leads Dan Sullivan by some six hundred votes in Alaska. Scott Colom beat Cindy Hyde-Smith by eleven hundred votes in Mississippi. Kansas, which had not elected a Democratic senator in living memory of anyone under a hundred, elected one. So did Texas. So did South Carolina. If the last two races fall, Democrats will have gained nine Senate seats in a single night -- one of the largest midterm swings in the modern history of the chamber.
That is not four-dimensional chess. That is the other side of the board winning in three...

subject: Walking with Destiny – Churchill, Character & Leadership Today

| Dear Friend,
This week, one of the greatest historians alive came to Jackson to talk about one of the greatest leaders who ever lived. Lord Andrew Roberts is the author of _Churchill: Walking with Destiny_ , and the first Churchill biographer allowed to use King George VI’s wartime diaries. Andrew took us back to May 10th, 1940 - the day Hitler unleashed Blitzkrieg on the West, and the day Churchill became prime minister. Churchill later wrote that all his past life had been but a preparation for that hour. It had. He survived many brushes with death - and he made more than his share of mistakes, above all the Dardanelles. What made him great was that he learned from his mistakes. He was almost alone in seeing Hitler for what he was. And when the establishment tried to shout him down through the 1930s, he did not change his message. He said it in short, plain words that everyone understood. Physical courage. Moral courage. Foresight. Eloquence. And a willingness to say what you believe, whether or not it wins you votes. Those qualities, Andrew agreed, are tremendously rare today. They are. Public life has no shortage of people with their ear to the ground. It has very few with the character to stand up and say what is true before it is popular. Churchill’s character was not handed to him in May 1940. It was formed over fifty years - by danger, by failure, by reading history, and by a decade out of office and out of favor. Leadership is what character looks like when the hour comes. The question for us is whether we are forming that kind of character in the next generation - and whether we will recognize it when we see it. We can have the most wonderful free market policies, produced by the cleverest think tanks in the world—but they count for nothing if we lack leaders with character. _Formerly All On The Line_

Peter, we need to talk about Black voter turnout in the South.
Black voters surged to the polls in Alabama, Mississippi, South Carolina, Louisiana, and Georgia. Take a look:
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143812189/661474279/-1059218283?refcode=don_aotl_tier1_email_BlackTurnoutAcrossSouth_email_20261121-AOTL-Tier1-BlackTurnoutAcrossSouth_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20261121-AOTL-Tier1-BlackTurnoutAcrossSouth_&utm_campaign=BlackTurnoutAcrossSouth&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjRmNjkyY2UyLWIzZTUtZjExMS05MWYzLTAwMGQzYTUzMzk3OCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=ap0VqzCGvTm4rsB9xgUL3D1msZf1hKmvDHu7_QU6778=)
---
This is a direct consequence of the cynical efforts to weaken Black voting power. As Attorney General Eric Holder put it: “If you look at what happened in the South after the Callais decision from the Supreme Court ... trying to take away Black representation, Latino representation ... it’s interesting to see what happened in this recent election. People said, we’re not going to take that. ... And we saw really huge turnout ... in African American populations and Latino populations.”
This is why we refused to cave when anti-democracy forces rushed to pass new gerrymanders across the South — shameful echoes of Jim Crow-style politics. We didn’t back down. We kept organizing. And voters weren’t shy about how they felt — they made their voices heard.
Progress can still happen when the odds are stacked against us. But we have to fight for it.
That’s why we’re more committed than ever to this work — the results of one election cycle don’t undo the damage done by racial gerrymandering across the South. And we know that some lawmakers aren’t done trying to pass the next. [ Donate today and let’s do everything we can to resist a new era of Jim Crow, together.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143812191/661474282/-1059218283?refcode=don_aotl_tier1_email_BlackTurnoutAcrossSouth_email_20261121-AOTL-Tier1-BlackTurnoutAcrossSouth_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20261121-AOTL-Tier1-BlackTurnoutAcrossSouth_&utm_campaign=BlackTurnoutAcrossSouth&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjRmNjkyY2UyLWIzZTUtZjExMS05MWYzLTAwMGQzYTUzMzk3OCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=ap0VqzCGvTm4rsB9xgUL3D1msZf1hKmvDHu7_QU6778=)

Black voters surged to the polls in Alabama, Mississippi, South Carolina, Louisiana, and Georgia. Take a look: = This is a direct consequence of the cynical efforts to weaken Black voting power. As Attorney General Eric Holder put it: “If you look at what happened in the South after the Callais decision from the Supreme Court ... trying to take away Black representation, Latino representation ... it’s interesting to see what happened in this recent election. People said, we’re not going to take that. ... And we saw really huge turnout ... in African American populations and Latino populations.” This is why we refused to cave when anti-democracy forces rushed to pass new gerrymanders across the South — shameful echoes of Jim Crow-style politics.
