| | Friends, As you know, Fair Fight was created to fight for vulnerable voters and defend democracy. **After a powerful and effective eight years, capped with deep and broad victories in Georgia and Mississippi in 2026, Fair Fight is undergoing a transition. The organization will conclude its current operations by the end of the year.** A new evolution to Stacey Abrams’ concept of a “Fair Fight” will be announced in 2027. **To our volunteers, donors, and supporters — thank you. Your dedicated work and funding has changed Georgia, the South and the nation, and has helped set the stage for this new political day in the United States. We are humbled and deeply grateful for your work and support through the years. It certainly has made a difference.** _The Fair Fight Story and Our Next Steps_ Fair Fight began in 2018 in response to unprecedented levels of voter suppression, and over the past eight years, we have been dedicated to spotlighting and defeating voter suppression nationwide, by advancing pro-voter policies, voter protection best practices and supporting pro democracy candidates across Georgia, the South and the nation. We defined voter suppression for the country in 2018 and 2019, and we built state-level operations that could push back and support voters against its onslaught in 2020 in 19 states across the country, from battlegrounds to Southern strongholds. In the process, we’ve consistently exposed bad actors and spearheaded litigation and legislative remedies. Whether in the courthouse, in the court of public opinion or behind the scenes to inform strategy, we’ve engaged at the point of voter needs to defend the right to vote. Using our breadth and strong volunteer base, we’ve won elections up and down the ballot and been instrumental in national and regional coalitions to advance voting rights; and in 2026, we helped convene a massive Southern cohort to push back against the racist and unjust SCOTUS Callais decision and support state leaders facing redrawing of maps across the region. Our efforts were critical in preventing 7 additional Black majority seats from being gutted by racist GOP leaders in spring and summer of 2026 who only managed to succeed in 3 of the 10 they attempted. Our efforts have helped to blunt the impact of voter suppression in all of its forms, force transparency on the problems and bad actors and advance positive changes for millions of American voters so they can have their voices heard and have words and support for navigating the disinformation, gaslighting and racism that current and historical voter suppression has wrought. For example, as a result of our litigation efforts, 22,000 voters were restored to the rolls in 2019 (twice the margin of victory in Georgia in 2020), a federal judge ruled Georgia’s felon match process in the voter registration system unconstitutional, and the state is taking steps to prevent new US Citizens (mostly people of color) from being falsely labeled as “ineligible.” Fair Fight, its coalition partners, and supporters are proud of this hard work that has helped to make Georgia and many other states more competitive in recent elections, including massive wins up and down the ballot that we’ve been a part of in 2020, 2021, 2024, 2025, and the recent 2026 midterms. In 2026, we saw through our mission that began when Stacey was Georgia House Minority Leader — a mission to not just win statewide in Georgia, but to win the Georgia State House and launch a new progressive policy vision for the state. Likewise, we have continued the Fair South mission with a group of organizations to build local partnerships and statewide victories in Mississippi and incubate opportunity elsewhere. _Next Steps_ **Fair Fight has met its mission: to be a champion in the battle for free and fair elections; and with such sweeping victories in Georgia and across our target states, we know it is time to write our next chapter.** This decision was not taken lightly; and in the coming months, we will ensure that where the fight continues, our allies are supported and that we honor our stakeholders. The 2026 midterm election results proved that change is possible. We see thousands of organizations operating nationally, in states and local communities making an impact. Our many coalition partners have grown over the past several years, and countless additional organizations protecting voter rights and defending our democracy have developed. We will ensure that all of our research, data, insights, materials, action plans and more are available to our partner organizations as resources for future efforts. As we look to the future, Stacey Abrams is spearheading a new evolution of Fair Fight — fighting authoritarianism at the state and local levels; she will be sharing more in 2027. To the talented Fair Fight team, past and present, we share our heartfelt gratitude for their service. The generational change we saw in the November elections is a reflection of your dedication to democracy, to each other, and to every eligible voter looking to make their voice heard at the ballot box. Your exceptional work showed that the South is ripe with possibility. You helped defy history, and reset the narrative for how we can create change. We will be working to support the team during this transition in several ways. This includes not only providing severance and other benefits, as well as helping them explore career next steps and placement opportunities. _Keep an eye out for more updates and news to come — we will not turn the page on this chapter until we have wrapped this up properly, and next year Stacey will be eager to share what is next for her new Fair Fight evolution, which I am cheering on as a friend. _ My best, Lauren Groh-Wargo
CEO, Fair Fight

clean_body: To our volunteers, donors, and supporters: thank you. Your dedicated work and funding has changed Georgia, the South and the nation, and has helped set the stage for this new political day in the United States. | | | Friends, As you know, Fair Fight was created to fight for vulnerable voters and defend democracy. After a powerful and effective eight years, capped with deep and broad victories in Georgia and Mississippi in 2026, Fair Fight is undergoing a transition. The organization will conclude its current operations by the end of the year. A new evolution to Stacey Abrams’ concept of a “Fair Fight” will be announced in 2027. To our volunteers, donors, and supporters — thank you. Your dedicated work and funding has changed Georgia, the South and the nation, and has helped set the stage for this new political day in the United States. We are humbled and deeply grateful for your work and support through the years. It certainly has made a difference. The Fair Fight Story and Our Next Steps Fair Fight began in 2018 in response to unprecedented levels of voter suppression, and over the past eight years, we have been dedicated to spotlighting and defeating voter suppression nationwide, by advancing pro-voter policies, voter protection best practices and supporting pro democracy candidates across Georgia, the South and the nation. We defined voter suppression for the country in 2018 and 2019, and we built state-level operations that could push back and support voters against its onslaught in 2020 in 19 states across the country, from battlegrounds to Southern strongholds. In the process, we’ve consistently exposed bad actors and spearheaded litigation and legislative remedies. Whether in the courthouse, in the court of public opinion or behind the scenes to inform strategy, we’ve engaged at the point of voter needs to defend the right to vote. Using our breadth and strong volunteer base, we’ve won elections up and down the ballot and been instrumental in national and regional coalitions to advance voting rights; and in 2026, we helped convene a massive Southern cohort to push back against the racist and unjust SCOTUS Callais decision and support state leaders facing redrawing of maps across the region. Our efforts were critical in preventing 7 additional Black majority seats from being gutted by racist GOP leaders in spring and summer of 2026 who only managed to succeed in 3 of the 10 they attempted. Our efforts have helped to blunt the impact of voter suppression in all of its forms, force transparency on the problems and bad actors and advance positive changes for millions of American voters so they can have their voices heard and have words and support for navigating the disinformation, gaslighting and racism that current and historical voter suppression has wrought. For example, as a result of our litigation efforts, 22,000 voters were restored to the rolls in 2019 (twice the margin of victory in Georgia in 2020), a federal judge ruled Georgia’s felon match process in the voter registration system unconstitutional, and the state is taking steps to prevent new US Citizens (mostly people of color) from being falsely labeled as “ineligible.” Fair Fight, its coalition partners, and supporters are proud of this hard work that has helped to make Georgia and many other states more competitive in recent elections, including massive wins up and down the ballot that we’ve been a part of in 2020, 2021, 2024, 2025, and the recent 2026 midterms. In 2026, we saw through our mission that began when Stacey was Georgia House Minority Leader — a mission to not just win statewide in Georgia, but to win the Georgia State House and launch a new progressive policy vision for the state. Likewise, we have continued the Fair South mission with a group of organizations to build local partnerships and statewide victories in Mississippi and incubate opportunity elsewhere. Next Steps Fair Fight has met its mission: to be a champion in the battle for free and fair elections; and with such sweeping victories in Georgia and across our target states, we know it is time to write our next chapter. This decision was not taken lightly; and in the coming months, we will ensure that where the fight continues, our allies are supported and that we honor our stakeholders. The 2026 midterm election results proved that change is possible. We see thousands of organizations operating nationally, in states and local communities making an impact. Our many coalition partners have grown over the past several years, and countless additional organizations protecting voter rights and defending our democracy have developed. We will ensure that all of our research, data, insights, materials, action plans and more are available to our partner organizations as resources for future efforts. As we look to the future, Stacey Abrams is spearheading a new evolution of Fair Fight — fighting authoritarianism at the state and local levels; she will be sharing more in 2027. To the talented Fair Fight team, past and present, we share our heartfelt gratitude for their service. The generational change we saw in the November elections is a reflection of your dedication to democracy, to each other, and to every eligible voter looking to make their voice heard at the ballot box. Your exceptional work showed that the South is ripe with possibility. You helped defy history, and reset the narrative for how we can create change. We will be working to support the team during this transition in several ways. This includes not only providing severance and other benefits, as well as helping them explore career next steps and placement opportunities. Keep an eye out for more updates and news to come — we will not turn the page on this chapter until we have wrapped this up properly, and next year Stacey will be eager to share what is next for her new Fair Fight evolution, which I am cheering on as a friend. Across this organization, we’re aligning on our priorities for 2027. We have an unprecedented opportunity ahead of us.
#

Team, we know you didn’t wake up this morning and think to yourself: Today is the day I’m going to make a donation to GIFFORDS.
But that’s what we’re about to ask you to do. And, if you give us a chance, we’d like to explain why that donation is so important. Especially now.
GIFFORDS invested $10 million across battleground races in the 2026 elections. We won in states and districts many pundits didn’t expect to be competitive. And we were able to do that because of the support of literally thousands of people, a massive network of grassroots supporters who fund our work.
And that work does not stop on Election Day.
Across this organization, we’re aligning on our priorities for 2027. We have an unprecedented opportunity ahead of us, and a tremendous amount of work to do in order to capitalize on it.
But one of the first fights we’ll have is in early December, when the Supreme Court will hear oral arguments in _Viramontes v. Cook County and Grant v. Higgins._
The Court’s decision will determine whether communities can come together to pass assault weapons bans, or whether those bans are illegal. The stakes couldn’t possibly be higher.
GIFFORDS has a huge role to play here, and we aren’t backing down from it.
That’s why this moment matters, and that’s why we’re hoping you’ll make a donation today. Because Gabby can’t do this alone.

subject: A scream through a hotel wall
body:
One little girl cried out for help. Someone listened. Now she’s safe.

| [View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e795876/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvamhadllycmRiMw/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMjE/LbmNsMFpyUzNEYg/qP2hpZHM9bmNkQUJ1dk56ZkRvMW1scw/gawGpBw/san45082296)
| | | [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
| |
---
| | God’s Children Are Not For Sale
---
|
---
| | | Friend,
---
Have you ever heard a sound you just couldn’t ignore?

For one woman staying in a hotel, it was the scream of a little girl on the other side of the wall.

I want to introduce you to “Daisy.”

But that’s not her real name. We’ll call her Daisy to protect her privacy.

And her story is why I am writing to you today.

My name is Eduardo Verástegui. I am the producer of the film _Sound of Freedom_ and the new movie _Zero A.D_.: The Birth of Christ, which hits theaters in December.

Years ago, I met rescuers who told me what really happens to children who are trafficked.

It broke my heart.

And it left me with a question I still can’t shake...

_What if it were my child_?
---
[ Rescue a Child — Give Now](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Hollywood said Sound of Freedom would never succeed.

Doors closed. Studios walked away.

**But we refused to give up.**

Because **God’s children are not for sale.**

body:
He was abusing his authority to silence voices he found inconvenient, even when that speech was protected by the First Amendment.
#

Team,
Last year, Pete Hegseth came after me. By doing so, he was trying to send a message to every retired member of the military: If you speak out and say something the President or the Secretary of Defense does not like, you could be censured, threatened with a reduction in retirement grade, or even prosecuted.
He was abusing his authority to silence voices he found inconvenient, even when that speech was protected by the First Amendment.
So, I took him to court. A federal judge heard the case and ruled in my favor, rejecting Hegseth’s arguments. And, before the ink was dry, Hegseth appealed.
We’ve been waiting on a ruling on that appeal ever since. We know it’s going to come, but we don’t know when. But whenever it does, we need to be ready to turn on a dime and respond.
What I keep coming back to is this: Hegseth didn’t need to appeal. He’s coming after me because Trump’s ordering to. He’s doing it in public, so every servicemember and veteran in the country can see it.
That’s the whole point. It was never just about me — it’s about making sure the next person thinks twice before they speak out.
I’m not going to let that happen, but I can’t do it on my own.

name: Major General Paul Eaton, U.S. Army, retired
subject: The Washington Post: “At the Tomb, Hegseth could not hear the silence that others hold sacred”
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY VOTEVETS, VOTEVETS
body:
#
Ladies and Gentlemen, this is Paul Eaton.
_The Washington Post_ just released an article about Pete Hegseth’s disgraceful conduct at Arlington National Cemetery. It talks about the Secretary of Defense’s actions, and what it can tell us about his character.
If you have a few minutes, I’ve attached the article for you to read. Thank you for your support of VoteVets.
| [DONATE](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-nov26.ldComW&refcode=em261121-1-misc&t=1&akid=35817%2E3013755%2E7CRSE9)
---

* * *

[](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-nov26.ldComW&refcode=em261121-1-misc&t=2&akid=35817%2E3013755%2E7CRSE9)
**At the Tomb, Hegseth could not hear the silence that others hold sacred**
[](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-nov26.ldComW&refcode=em261121-1-misc&t=3&akid=35817%2E3013755%2E7CRSE9)
After the carnage of World War I, Americans grieved particularly for the soldiers whose bodies were left behind in France, and for the several thousand whose remains were never identified. It was a political issue, a cultural wound and it changed how we memorialized the fallen, from a local to a national duty. The Tomb of the Unknowns at Arlington National Cemetery, where Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and his entourage were admonished Wednesday for acting disrespectfully, was a response to that trauma.
The slaughter of the Great War, a fratricidal conflict of European monarchies, created overwhelming public disgust in England and France. Governments there responded to the outrage with a postwar show of egalitarianism, honoring an anonymous soldier with the highest honors and burial at Westminster Abbey in England and at the Arc de Triomphe in France. The United States, which hired its best architects to create cemeteries in France and considered creating a memorial forest north of Washington, followed the lead of its European allies and honored the unidentified dead with its own Tomb of the Unknown Soldier in 1921.
[](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-nov26.ldComW&refcode=em261121-1-misc&t=4&akid=35817%2E3013755%2E7CRSE9)
That’s where Hegseth, his wife and a gaggle of senior staff laughed, joked and bantered as if they were at a garden party, on the 11th day of the 11th month, once known as Armistice Day and now the day set aside to honor America’s veterans. Their boorish behavior, at a place where silence is strictly enjoined, was reprimanded by one of the army sentinels from The Old Guard, who upbraided them with the usual formula: “All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times.”
Hegseth responded to that reprimand Thursday by honoring the soldier who shouted it, Spc. Thomas Iglesias, with the Joint Service Commendation Medal, commending the “execution of his duties at the Tomb of the Unknowns on November 11, 2026.”
The Tomb of the Unknowns, which now includes remains from later conflicts, sits on a plaza in front of the imposing facade of Arlington Memorial Amphitheater. The stone paving and the masonry building amplify the sound of the guards, whose dress shoes have metal plates that make a sharp clicking sound as they finish their 21-step ceremonial march. The changing of the guard, every half hour during the warm months of the year, has its own sonic profile, with sharp taps on stone and the percussive sounds of the Relief Commander inspecting the sentinel’s rifle.
These are “earcons,” an idea discussed in a book about architecture and sound, “Spaces Speak, Are you Listening?” by Barry Blesser, a former MIT professor, and independent scholar Linda-Ruth Salter. An earcon is “the aural analogue of a visual icon,” they write, “a sonic event that contains special symbolic meaning not present in the sound wave.” An earcon might be the family dinner bell, or the particular resonance of a cathedral or the crowing of a cock at sunrise.
[](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-nov26.ldComW&refcode=em261121-1-misc&t=5&akid=35817%2E3013755%2E7CRSE9)
Members of the 3rd U.S. Infantry Regiment, known as "The Old Guard," during a changing of the guard ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknowns in Arlington, Virginia. (Bill O'Leary/The Washington Post)
And most certainly, it is the sharp but subtle sound of the guards at the Tomb of the Unknowns, where the vast majority of onlookers feel a sense of awe and gratitude and need no reminder that silence is the highest form of respect. Social media is full of video of crowds gathered to watch the sentinel’s stately march and the changing of the guard. They are often tourists, dressed like tourists, with the tourist’s restless stance and compulsive need to take pictures. And yet, even in these amateur videos, the earcon of the sentinels creates a quasi-sacred sonic space, a rhythmic sound set against silence, conjuring both the repose of the dead and the passage of time.
Video of Hegseth’s ill-mannered display doesn’t capture the full impact of its disruption because the voices are too far from the camera’s microphone. But it does capture the full resonance of the sentinel’s booming response, which is deeply moving. An ordinary soldier, on behalf of those who have died for their country, demands respect from the man who styles himself the Secretary of War, a man who administers the executive’s life or death power over those who serve, no matter their rank.
Since the first tombs that honored a symbolic, nameless soldier after World War I, countries around the world, democratic, autocratic and totalitarian, have created tombs for the unknown dead. It’s reassuring that in America, despite its flirtation with authoritarianism, would-be authoritarians are still subject to the rules of decorum at Arlington National Cemetery.
[](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-nov26.ldComW&refcode=em261121-1-misc&t=6&akid=35817%2E3013755%2E7CRSE9)
Visitors gather at the Tomb of the Unknowns to witness a changing of the guard ceremony. (Bill O'Leary/The Washington Post)
Silence, as a form of respect, is particularly social, selfless and engaged. Raising a flag — or wearing one as a pocket square — is performative. Like singing the anthem or saying the Pledge of Allegiance, it is easily done. One can always put out more flags. These are acts made for public display and to some degree they are designed to call attention to one’s own show of patriotism.
Silence is other-oriented. A respectful silence — at a place of worship, in a concert hall or at the Tomb in Arlington — shifts the focus from the individual to the collective. Silence is created by multiple small acts of self-discipline, which become an analogue for self-sacrifice; yet that silence can be shattered by a single lout, narcissist or buffoon.
That Hegseth didn’t care enough on Veterans Day to honor veterans with just a little silence at Arlington should surprise no one. He is a showman who enacts a parody of masculine bravado and bellicosity for an increasingly small audience. Laughing and chatting in front of the tomb was not an isolated lapse of protocol or decorum; it was a display of power, the power of people indifferent to rules, through noise and spectacle, a power so self-conceited it can’t hear the silence that others hold sacred.
[](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-nov26.ldComW&refcode=em261121-1-misc&t=7&akid=35817%2E3013755%2E7CRSE9)
Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Gen. Dan Caine, left, Jennifer Hegseth and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth watch a wreath-laying ceremony on Veterans Day last year at The Tomb of the Unknowns. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)
One might extend that to the entire Trump administration, to the giant triumphal arch with which President Donald Trump would assert his personal presence at the edge of Arlington to the visual cacophony he has made of the now ornamented and gilded Oval Office, or the UFC match and car race last summer that made the nation’s monuments mere backdrop for noisy spectacle. Silence is simply a vacuum, a space to be filled; it is the darkness before someone turns on the spotlight and the show begins.
In the dreadful 2020 movie based on Vice President JD Vance’s memoir “Hillbilly Elegy,” the young JD asks his Mamaw why the townsfolk are quietly saluting his grandfather’s funeral procession: “Because, honey, we’re hill people. And we respect our dead.”
It isn’t just hill people who respect their dead. And those who have served and died for their country deserve a particular respect. It’s good to have a reminder of what respect means, when and to whom it is owed, what it sounds like, and what kind of man considers himself above the obligation.
No one should expect any better of Hegseth, who is what he is. But as the nation turns a corner and Trumpism begins to wane, we can be thankful for this: The last two years have been an astonishing civics lesson.
* * *

VoteVets is on the front lines to support our Veterans and stand up against Donald Trump’s corruption in his last two years, but we need your help.
If everyone reading this donated just $10, we could have the resources to continue our important work for this year and beyond.
**If $10 seems worth it to you to continue going toe-to-toe with Trump and MAGA Republicans everywhere, then please contribute to VoteVets today.**

Friend,

Last week, mid-Michigan sent me back to Congress – and this time, I’ll be serving in a new Democratic majority. Thank you, truly, for placing your trust in me.

* * *
I can already hear the whining from the MAGA media machine.
The Democratic investigations are coming, and they're going to be wide-reaching. They have to be. They have to include members of the Trump crime family, the relatives of cabinet officials, and everyone else in this administration who has used the power of the federal government to line their own pockets.
Because everywhere you turn, the grift is unbelievable.
Jared Kushner, the president's son-in-law and probably the most corrupt member of his own family (which is really saying something), is investing in weapons manufacturers while he's supposedly negotiating peace. He is the most compromised man in the Trump administration. His investment firm is essentially taking bribes from foreign governments in exchange for favors from Washington, particularly for countries in the Middle East. You can't trust a single thing he says or does, because it all serves one goal: getting as rich as possible before he and his father-in-law get kicked out of office.
Then there's Trump's kids, with their crypto scams and their government contracts. There's Ivanka, building the new Epstein island, a luxury playground for the ultra-rich on a protected island off the coast of Albania. Howard Lutnick's family firm went looking to cash in on his own tariffs getting struck down in court, the same tariffs he was out there selling to the American people.
And it goes all the way down to the spouses. Todd Blanche, the Attorney General of the United States, has a wife peddling unproven cures online. Stephen and Katie Miller live on a taxpayer-funded military base, throwing lavish parties, because they're too scared to go out into the real world and get booed for the lives they've ruined. Pete Hegseth's wife, Jennifer, has been paid by a firm that works for one of the Pentagon's biggest contractors, and she follows her husband around helping him run the place because he's too compromised to do the job himself.
Oh, and Barron Trump is friends with infamous human trafficker Andrew Tate.
On and on and on. And that's just the stuff we know about. That's just what I could remember sitting down to write this on a Saturday morning before the college football games kick off.

These tariffs are driving up the cost of everything because of the corruption. Every time you wince at the grocery store, you're paying the Trump family tax.
Democrats were given a directive in the election earlier this month. Not a mandate. A directive. Fix it. Make a material difference in people's lives. People are working so goddamn hard just to live with some dignity, to take care of their families, to take a vacation, to retire with enough money to actually enjoy it. The only way we deliver for them is by breaking this corrupt cabal.
So yes, there will be whiners. There will be bad-faith actors paid to bitch and moan about Democrats doing exactly what we were sent to do. I don't care. It doesn't matter if you're the President of the United States, a cabinet secretary, a janitor at the White House, or somebody's son-in-law. If you abused your power and stole from the American people, you answer for it.
And nobody should be safe. Democrat or Republican, family member or not. I don't want to hear any of that shit. This didn't start with Donald Trump. It's been going on for a long time. It's just gotten so craven that nobody can look away anymore. Everybody in the Epstein files who committed a crime should be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. Everybody who abused their power to line their pockets, same thing. Every member of Congress engaged in insider trading should be exposed, and congressional insider trading should be outlawed.
I'm a proud Democrat. I'll probably be one until the day I die, as long as it's the party fighting for working people and not for a handful of corrupt billionaires. But goddamn it, there's corruption in my party too, and I want to weed it all out. That's why I said yesterday that no Democrat should take a dime from Elon Musk. And we shouldn't buy this sudden pivot from Big Tech, as if they've been progressive all along. They cheered on everything Trump did for two years and joined the grift to pump their stock prices. They're tanking the economy, and we're the ones paying for it.
Here's the thing. Plenty of people in Congress, in both parties, know exactly how rotten Washington is right now. They're playing a game of chicken, waiting to see who blinks. Whichever party moves first, and passes the most sweeping campaign finance and ethics reform this country has ever seen, ends Citizens United, bans insider trading, and makes sure this level of grift can never happen again, will be rewarded by the American people. I believe that party will govern for a very long time.
I've been in politics for about two decades. Every election but one has been a change election, with the American people crying out for relief as everything keeps getting worse. If Democrats are serious about these investigations, and we do them for the right reasons, we can lay the foundation for a massive win in 2028 and prepare the country for what it's going to take to make sure this never happens again.
But only if we can stomach the hard choices. Only if we stand on business, stand on our values, and let the new generation of leaders who came in calling out this corruption actually lead.
Generational change is here. Let's make it count. Let's get to work.
With urgency,
--Mike

body:
Truth to Power is making it easier for the next generation of progressive leaders to win.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=41649%2E3422442%2EeP9-1r)
Peter,
Looking back at this election, I’m proud of how this team stepped up to support the candidates on our 2026 slate. **Truth to Power raised money directly for progressive leaders running in some of the most important races in the country, helping them win.**
We raised thousands for champions like Abdul El-Sayed and Troy Jackson—money they used to counter _massive_ spending from outside groups. In smaller races, we gave candidates like Marni von Wilpert an early boost that put them in a position to win once polls opened.
We repeated this playbook across the map: Josh Turek, Sam Forstag, Cait Conley, Randy Villegas, and many more received direct support from Truth to Power and won their races. These champions helped us take back Congress and will make sure the agenda reflects the needs of working families, not billionaires and corporations.
**This is how we build power in the Capitol for everyday people: find leaders ready to fight for families struggling to get by, and give them the resources to win.**
I saw firsthand how difficult flipping a Republican seat is when I did it in 2018. Truth to Power is making that process easier for the next generation of leaders so we can elect even more of them in the future.
**[You helped us win these races, Peter, and we need you with us to keep building momentum. Can you donate $5 or more to help us get ready to support more candidates in 2028?](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20261121_1_ak.yk5e23&refcode=em20261121-41649&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=41649%2E3422442%2EeP9-1r)**
[Donate ›››](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20261121_1_ak.yk5e23&refcode=em20261121-41649&t=21&akid=41649%2E3422442%2EeP9-1r)
Thank you,
Katie

Former U.S. Congresswoman Katie Porter founded Truth to Power to support the campaigns of her fellow Democrats. Truth to Power supports candidates who will stand up to Donald Trump, fight to lower costs, and protect the environment. **[Donate ›››](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/truth-to-power-1?refcode=em20261121-41649&amounts=&t=22&refcode2=41649_3422442_eP9-1r&akid=41649%2E3422442%2EeP9-1r)**

body:
[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/18910?refcode=em20261121-2970-foote&t=1001&akid=2970%2E342411%2EUt1TWg ]Squad Victory Fund

Peter, just weeks
before Election Day, Donald Trump’s DHS agents raided Ilhan’s home in a
blatant attempt to intimidate her.

Now Trump’s administration is trying to strip Ilhan of the citizenship
she’s held for more than 25 years, using claims that have been debunked
again and again.

This is the latest escalation in Trump’s relentless revenge campaign
against Ilhan.

Why? Because Ilhan stands up for working people and refuses to back down.
In coming after her, Trump has put Ilhan, our Squad, and the people and
communities they love and represent in danger.

Trump’s playbook is simple: use fear to shut down progressive power. He’s
trying to make an example out of the Squad so no one else dares to speak
up.

But we know what this movement is made of, and we won’t be intimidated.
With threats this serious, security isn’t optional. It’s what lets our
Squad keep fighting in Congress.

We refuse to let Ilhan face these attacks alone, and we’re counting on
grassroots supporters like you to step up. We need to make sure the Squad
has the security they need to stay safe and unapologetically fearless in
the halls of Congress.

next?

The Squad Victory Fund

name: What's Next w/ Our Revolution
subject: Democrats Won on Affordability. Time for a Living Wage for ALL!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Our Revolution click here to unsubscribe
body:
[ stdin# ]Our Revolution Logo

Peter Willis,

Democrats just won new majorities in Congress. Now it's time to deliver
for working people.

The federal minimum wage has been stuck at a poverty-level $7.25 an hour
since 2009. That's 17 years without a raise — while the cost of housing,
groceries, healthcare, and just about everything else has skyrocketed.

Meanwhile, corporate profits have soared, billionaires have gotten
obscenely rich, and workers have been left behind.

It's time for Congress to pass the Living Wage for All Act and raise the
federal minimum wage to $25 an hour.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40144?t=1011&akid=11622%2E5885482%2EOc32MI ]SIGN THE PETITION: DEMAND A $25 LIVING WAGE!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40144?t=1012&akid=11622%2E5885482%2EOc32MI ]Headline: Democrats could raise the minimum wage next year. How high
should they go?

Here's how badly the system is failing working people:

* Since 1979, worker productivity has gone up 92% while wages have risen
by 34%.
* If the minimum wage had kept pace with inflation and productivity
since 1968, it would have reached $25 an hour by 2023.
* In 20 states, the minimum wage is still just $7.25 an hour — nowhere
near enough to support a family.

Working people are producing more wealth than ever. So why aren't they
sharing in it?

The Living Wage for All Act would begin raising the minimum wage
immediately — from $7.25 to $12 in the first year — and establish a path
to $25 an hour, with large corporate employers reaching that floor by
2032.

It would also phase out subminimum wages for tipped workers, workers with
disabilities, and young workers, and ensure wages continue rising with the
national median wage.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40144?t=1013&akid=11622%2E5885482%2EOc32MI ]ADD YOUR NAME: PASS THE LIVING WAGE FOR ALL ACT!

Our Revolution helped mobilize millions of voter contacts to flip Congress
because government should work for working people — not just billionaire
donors and corporate CEOs.

Now Democrats have the power to act.

No more excuses. No more poverty wages. No more telling working families
to wait while the wealthy get richer.

If you work full-time, you should be able to afford a decent home, put
food on the table, and live with dignity.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40144?t=1014&akid=11622%2E5885482%2EOc32MI ]Tell Democrats to use their new majorities to pass the Living Wage for
All Act and make a $25 living wage a reality.

When we organize, we win.

Our Revolution

| | Hey Peter, I know you take time to read the emails we send, and I really appreciate it. I’m reaching out because the next phase of our year-round organizing program is already underway. Across Florida, our team is preparing to launch our next student fellowship program, register more voters, and plan more community events that bring people together. **This work can’t stop between election cycles, and neither can our fundraising. That’s why, during this time especially, we rely heavily on monthly recurring donations.** This sustained support between elections helps us retain year-round staff, plan consistent door-knocking and community events, connect with voters year-round, and keep our Florida organizing HQ open without starting from zero each election. By building trust, collecting feedback, and staying connected with you throughout the year, we can keep moving forward on the progress we’ve made in 2026. Our organizing is entirely supported by people like you who believe in bold, transformational change. subject: [take action] Demand governors take immediate action to prevent Medicaid and SNAP cuts

Friend, **Our fight to reverse the harm done by congressional Republicans doesn’t need to wait until new Democratic majorities are sworn in in January. Our communities need support now.** When Republicans passed their Big Betrayal Bill in 2025, they slashed critical programs like Medicaid and SNAP to hand tax breaks to billionaires and corporations. It’s estimated that if Medicaid work-reporting requirements go into effect, **10 million people could lose their health care coverage****.** And since passage of the bill, **5.5 million people have already lost nutrition assistance** , including millions of kids. But right now, our governors can take action to protect people who rely on Medicaid and SNAP. For the next three weeks, the administration is allowing governors to sign onto a 6-month delay in Medicaid work-reporting requirements. And hopefully in that window, our new Democratic-controlled Congress can do away with them entirely. Most people on Medicaid already work, but often in jobs with inconsistent hours, making it hard to meet Republicans’ new reporting requirements. # How to Set Separate Alarm and Ringer Volumes on Your iPhone
Apple has finally rolled out a long-awaited capability: iPad and iPhone users can now set separate volumes for their ringtones and alarms. Here's how to set the alarm volume on your iPhone separate from your ringer volume.
## Why You'll Love This Tip
* **Set a wake-up alarm that doesn't make you jump out of your skin when it goes off.**
* **Set a ringtone alarm that you can hear regardless of ambient noise volume.**

## How to Adjust Ringer Volume on Your iPhone Independently of Alarm Volume
### System Requirements
_This tip was tested on an iPhone 17 running iOS 27. These steps do not work for users running iOS 26. Find out how to update to the_ _[latest version of iOS](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-261950-8633363-caa57e7640-9t49b694e0)_ _._ Want a quieter wake-up alarm, but a louder phone volume on your iPhone? Here's how to change the volume of the alarm on your iPhone separate from the ringer in a few easy steps.
1. Open the **Settings app**.

|
---
2. Tap **Sounds & Haptics**.

---
3. Toggle off **Match Ringtone Volume** under**Alarms and Timers**.**** Now, you can set your alarm volume to a different volume than your ringer.

---
### Enjoying Your Tip of the Day?
If you'd like to learn more about iPhone Life's premium paid subscription, [click here](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-261950-3303027-1fd3a5b59c-9t49b694e0)
4. You can also toggle off **Match Ringtone Volume** under **Alerts and System Sounds**. When you do this, you can change the sound level for alerts for incoming texts and system sounds.

---

Now you know how to set different alarm and ringtone volumes on your iPhone and iPad. Be sure to check out our free [Tip of the Day](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-261950-8633364-0b0653df63-9t49b694e0) for more iPhone alarm and ringtone tutorials.
